This compact set of image-space anchor points serves as a universal interface for diverse tasks, including point-goal, object-goal, poi-goal, instruction-following, and person-following. Subsequently, a fast action expert leverages both the textual cues and the pixel guidance to generate continuous waypoints at the native control frequency. By bridging high-level intents and low-level control through pixel-grounded anchors paired with explicit linguistic traces, our approach ensures robust, generalizable, and interpretable navigation across simulation and real-world benchmarks. ABot-N1 establishes new state-of-the-art records, delivering massive gains specifically in urban-scale navigation: boosting POI arrival by 35.0% (to 77.3%) and achieving 95.4%/92.9% SR in complex indoor and outdoor scenes. It also maintains superior robustness across object-reaching, person-following, and instruction-following tasks. New Point-Goal/POI-Goal benchmarks are released as open source to advance the field of urban-scale navigation.

AI.tldr: ABot-N1 is a Visual Language Navigation foundation model that decouples cognition from control using a slow-fast architecture. A slow vision-language reasoner performs Chain-of-Thought reasoning to produce pixel goals (image-space anchor points), while a fast action expert generates continuous waypoints. This achieves robust, interpretable navigation across diverse tasks, setting new SOTA with 35.0% improvement in POI arrival (77.3%) and 95.4%/92.9% Success Rate in complex indoor/outdoor scenes.
AI.motivation: Existing Visual Language Navigation foundation models use monolithic policies that map observations directly to actions, suffering from coordinate drift, poor handling of long-tail semantics, and lack of interpretability. The challenge is achieving generality, robustness, and transparency simultaneously.
AI.method: ABot-N1 employs a slow-fast architecture: (1) a slow vision-language reasoner performs explicit Chain-of-Thought reasoning to output a pixel goal (image-space anchor points), serving as a universal interface across diverse tasks; (2) a fast action expert uses both textual cues and pixel guidance to generate continuous waypoints at native control frequency.
AI.result: New SOTA: 35.0% improvement in POI arrival (to 77.3%), 95.4%/92.9% SR in complex indoor/outdoor scenes. Superior robustness across object-reaching, person-following, and instruction-following tasks. New Point-Goal/POI-Goal benchmarks released as open source.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling cognition from control via pixel-grounded anchors paired with explicit linguistic traces enables robust, generalizable, and interpretable navigation across simulation and real-world benchmarks, advancing urban-scale navigation.

title: AI YOU Town: Make Friends and Money with Your Digital Twin
summary: Existing approaches to infer user traits and generate responses consistent with a persona rely on static prompting. They lack calibrated uncertainty, ignore sequential evidence, and drift during long interactions. We present \textbf{AI YOU}, a framework that continually updates a personality profile with 22 dimensions from conversation and embodies it in a personal digital twin. Practically, the system combines prompting, Bayesian updating, and conformal prediction for persona inference. A periodically refreshed memory anchor and cognitive memory with three layers preserve persona consistency over long interactions. Across the main results, AI YOU \emph{(i)} achieves conformal coverage ranging from 0.921 to 0.976, \emph{(ii)} improves uncertainty calibration and reasoning grounded in memory, and \emph{(iii)} enhances persona fidelity over static prompting in role playing over 100 turns while reducing trait drift, for most evaluated backbones under adversarial settings with multiple agents. The prototype \emph{AI YOU Town} initializes an imaginative twin world for future interaction. The online demo is available at \href{https://quinnnnnne-ai-you.hf.space/}{\mbox{\texttt{quinnnnnne-ai-you.hf.space}}}.

AI.tldr: AI YOU is a framework that continually updates a 22-dimension personality profile from conversation using Bayesian updating and conformal prediction, with a multi-layer memory system to maintain persona consistency over long interactions, achieving high conformal coverage (0.921-0.976) and reducing trait drift in role-playing over 100 turns.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches for inferring user traits and generating persona-consistent responses rely on static prompting, which lacks calibrated uncertainty, ignores sequential evidence, and suffers from drift during long interactions.
AI.method: The framework combines prompting, Bayesian updating, and conformal prediction for continual persona inference. It uses a periodically refreshed memory anchor and a three-layer cognitive memory to preserve persona consistency over long interactions.
AI.result: AI YOU achieves conformal coverage from 0.921 to 0.976, improves uncertainty calibration and reasoning grounded in memory, and enhances persona fidelity over static prompting in role-playing over 100 turns while reducing trait drift across most evaluated backbones under adversarial multi-agent settings.
AI.conclusion: The system effectively addresses key limitations of static persona inference; a prototype AI YOU Town is initialized for future interactions, with an online demo available.

title: PhysMRV: Physical Memory Retrieval and Verification for Physics Plausibility Reasoning
summary: Video-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable performance on video understanding and visual question answering, yet they remain unreliable in reasoning about physical plausibility, where understanding object interactions, causal dynamics, and fundamental physical principles is essential. This limitation is particularly evident on challenging physical reasoning benchmarks, revealing a persistent gap in physical commonsense reasoning. To address this challenge, we propose PhysMRV, a training-free physical memory and verification framework for physical plausibility reasoning. Unlike retrieval-augmented VLMs that retrieve semantically similar videos as additional context, PhysMRV transforms training videos into a Hierarchical Memory Bank of structured physical knowledge comprising three complementary levels: scene descriptions capturing visual context, physical-event graphs modeling object interactions and causal structure, and physics-rule summaries distilling reusable physical principles and cues. During inference, PhysMRV retrieves physically relevant memories and leverages their structured physical evidence to guide a frozen VLM in verifying physical plausibility, requiring neither fine-tuning nor parameter updates. We evaluate PhysMRV on three challenging physical reasoning benchmarks, ImplausiBench, IntPhys2, and GRASP Level 2, across multiple state-of-the-art VLMs. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements over direct prompting across diverse VLMs and evaluation benchmarks, showing that structured physical memories provide an effective and scalable means of enhancing physical plausibility reasoning without additional training.

AI.tldr: PhysMRV is a training-free framework that enhances video-language models' physical plausibility reasoning by transforming training videos into a structured Hierarchical Memory Bank (scene descriptions, physical-event graphs, physics-rule summaries) and using retrieved physical evidence to guide frozen VLMs during inference, achieving consistent improvements on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Video-language models struggle with physical plausibility reasoning (object interactions, causal dynamics, physical principles), showing a persistent gap on challenging physical reasoning benchmarks despite strong performance on general video understanding tasks.
AI.method: PhysMRV constructs a Hierarchical Memory Bank from training videos with three levels: (1) scene descriptions for visual context, (2) physical-event graphs for object interactions and causal structure, and (3) physics-rule summaries for reusable physical principles. During inference, it retrieves physically relevant memories and uses their structured evidence to guide a frozen VLM—no fine-tuning or parameter updates required.
AI.result: Evaluated on ImplausiBench, IntPhys2, and GRASP Level 2 across multiple state-of-the-art VLMs, PhysMRV consistently outperforms direct prompting baselines, demonstrating that structured physical memories improve physical plausibility reasoning without additional training.
AI.conclusion: Structured physical memories provide an effective and scalable means of enhancing physical commonsense reasoning in VLMs, eliminating the need for fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation with semantically similar videos.

title: Vertical Fusion: Condensing Internal Representations for Robust ViT Classification
summary: Despite exposing rich intermediate representations, Vision Transformers (ViTs) are almost exclusively utilized as black-box feature extractors, where only the last layer is considered for downstream tasks. We challenge this convention by introducing the notion of recoverability: the capacity of intermediate representations to correct last-layer failures. By evaluating independent classification probes at every model depth across 16 datasets, we observe that intermediate probes correctly classify 18% to 76% of samples that the last-layer probe misclassifies. We show that these gains are not primarily driven by predictive diversity, but by a redundancy-correctness correspondence, where the internal hierarchy acts as a series of stable, redundant probes of a shared discriminative signal. While established horizontal ensemble strategies (i.e., across multiple models) can improve performance, they incur high computational cost and ignore this vertical signal within a single model. To bridge this gap, we propose VFusion, a principled vertical aggregation strategy employing a learnable mapping into a low-dimensional latent space that synthesizes features across the internal ViT hierarchy. VFusion substantially outperforms established aggregation baselines in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings, notably closing 45% of the accuracy gap between the best individual layer and a theoretical oracle performance. Our gains consistently generalize across model sizes and pre-training regimes, confirming that VFusion offers a robust and efficient alternative to horizontal ensemble methods. The code is available at https://github.com/francescodisalvo05/vit-vertical-fusion.

AI.tldr: ViTs are used only as black-box feature extractors, but intermediate layers can correct last-layer failures (18%-76% improvement). The paper proposes VFusion, a vertical aggregation method that fuses internal ViT features, closing 45% of the gap between the best individual layer and an oracle, outperforming horizontal ensembles at lower cost.
AI.motivation: ViTs are typically used as black-box feature extractors where only the last layer is considered. The authors challenge this by introducing "recoverability" — the ability of intermediate representations to correct last-layer failures — and aim to exploit this vertical signal efficiently.
AI.method: The authors define recoverability, evaluate independent probes at every depth across 16 datasets, analyze the redundancy-correctness correspondence, and propose VFusion — a learnable mapping into a low-dimensional latent space that aggregates features across the ViT hierarchy.
AI.result: Intermediate probes correctly classify 18%-76% of last-layer misclassifications; VFusion closes 45% of the accuracy gap between the best individual layer and an oracle; gains generalize across model sizes and pre-training regimes; outperforms established aggregation baselines in both in-distribution and OOD settings.
AI.conclusion: VFusion offers a robust and efficient alternative to horizontal ensemble methods by leveraging the internal ViT hierarchy as redundant, stable discriminative signals, providing substantial gains without the high computational cost of ensembling multiple models.

title: Large language model agents accelerate inverse design of metal-organic frameworks for gas separation
summary: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a highly modular platform for adsorptive gas separation, yet their vast reticular design space makes inverse design difficult under simultaneous constraints of chemical validity, separation performance, and structural diversity. Here, we present LEMO Agent, a large-language-model agent framework for closed-loop inverse design of gas-separation MOFs in MOFid space. LEMO Agent couples language-based candidate generation with MOFid standardization, explicit validity checking, Transformer-based property prediction, structured design memory, and multi-island exploration. Through iterative generate--validate--evaluate--remember cycles, the agent uses feedback from both successful and failed candidates to guide chemically constrained search across linker, metal, and topology choices. We evaluate LEMO Agent on CH$_4$/N$_2$ and CO$_2$/N$_2$ separation tasks. Compared with representative generative, optimization, and agentic baselines, LEMO Agent enriches high-performing candidates, improves predicted separation performance, and maintains broad chemical and topological diversity. Selected candidates are further reconstructed, evaluated by GCMC simulations, and passed through an experimental down-selection workflow based on chemical feasibility and ligand purchasability, leading to initial wet-lab synthesis and SEM characterization. These results demonstrate that large language model agents can serve as interpretable and scalable design engines for accelerating MOF discovery beyond conventional fixed-library screening.

AI.tldr: LEMO Agent is a closed-loop LLM-based framework that iteratively generates, validates, and evaluates gas-separation MOFs in MOFid space, outperforming baselines on CH₄/N₂ and CO₂/N₂ separation tasks, with experimental synthesis validation.
AI.motivation: MOFs offer modular gas separation platforms, but their vast reticular design space makes inverse design difficult under simultaneous constraints of chemical validity, separation performance, and structural diversity.
AI.method: LLM-based agent (LEMO Agent) coupling candidate generation via language, MOFid standardization, validity checking, Transformer-based property prediction, structured design memory, and multi-island exploration in iterative generate–validate–evaluate–remember cycles.
AI.result: LEMO Agent enriches high-performing candidates, improves predicted separation performance, and maintains chemical/topological diversity on CH₄/N₂ and CO₂/N₂ tasks, with selected candidates validated via GCMC, experimental down-selection, wet-lab synthesis, and SEM characterization.
AI.conclusion: LLM agents can serve as interpretable and scalable design engines for accelerating MOF discovery beyond conventional fixed-library screening.

title: Generative Augmentation of Raman Spectra for Glioma Classification
summary: Access to sufficiently large biomedical datasets remains a major obstacle for machine learning in Raman spectroscopy-based diagnostics. In particular, for glioma analysis, datasets are typically small and heterogeneous, affected by acquisition-specific variability. This work investigates the utility of deep generative augmentation in such a small-cohort setting. We analyze glioma biopsy spectra acquired from 58 tumor samples and consider both binary IDH-status classification and 6-class methylation subtype classification problems. To address the limited size and imbalance of the dataset, we develop a conditional variational autoencoder ($β$-CVAE) capable of generating class-conditioned synthetic Raman spectra. The generated data are evaluated in Train-on-Synthetic, Test-on-Real (TS/TR) and Train-on-Synthetic+Real, Test-on-Real (TSR/TR) settings under a strict patient-isolated cross-validation protocol. Models trained exclusively on synthetic data underperform models trained on real spectra, indicating a substantial domain gap between synthetic and real distributions. However, augmenting the real training data with synthetic spectra consistently improves classification performance across multiple models. These findings indicate that, even with a limited number of independent patient samples, generative models can capture sufficient structure to provide useful regularization for downstream classifiers. We also investigate a reconstruction-based inference strategy, termed Classification by Reconstruction (CbR), in which class prediction is based on reconstruction error under different class conditions. Overall, the results support the use of deep generative augmentation as a practical strategy for improving machine learning robustness in Raman spectroscopy applications characterized by limited biomedical datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates using a conditional variational autoencoder (β-CVAE) to generate synthetic Raman spectra for augmenting small, imbalanced biomedical datasets. On a glioma dataset of 58 tumor samples, synthetic data augmentation consistently improves classification performance across multiple models for IDH-status and methylation subtype tasks, despite a domain gap between synthetic and real spectra.
AI.motivation: Access to sufficiently large biomedical datasets is a major obstacle for machine learning in Raman spectroscopy-based diagnostics, particularly for glioma analysis where datasets are small and heterogeneous due to acquisition-specific variability.
AI.method: A conditional variational autoencoder (β-CVAE) generates class-conditioned synthetic Raman spectra. Evaluation uses Train-on-Synthetic, Test-on-Real (TS/TR) and Train-on-Synthetic+Real, Test-on-Real (TSR/TR) settings under strict patient-isolated cross-validation. A reconstruction-based inference strategy called Classification by Reconstruction (CbR) is also investigated.
AI.result: Models trained exclusively on synthetic data underperform those trained on real data, indicating a domain gap. However, augmenting real training data with synthetic spectra consistently improves classification performance across multiple models. The CbR strategy also shows utility.
AI.conclusion: Even with limited independent patient samples, generative models can capture sufficient structure to provide useful regularization. Deep generative augmentation is a practical strategy for improving ML robustness in Raman spectroscopy with limited biomedical datasets.

title: Self-supervised Automatic Matting
summary: High-quality alpha mattes are notoriously expensive to annotate, creating a fundamental data bottleneck for deep image matting. While prior work attempts to reduce annotation cost using coarser labels like trimaps or masks, they remain reliant on costly per-pixel supervision, limiting scalability and generalization. In this work, we push the boundary further and ask: can we train an automatic matting model using only RGB images, with no manual annotation at all? We answer this by presenting SSMatte, a self-supervised framework that for the first time achieves performance on par with fully-supervised automatic matting. Our key insight is to decompose the problem into semantic anchoring and detail matting. SSMatte first generates a semantic matting prompt from frozen self-supervised ViT features by propagating class-token seeds via a novel, training-efficient semantic anchoring loss based on a generalized Rayleigh quotient. This prompt then anchors a detail matting network, which is optimized via a fixed-point-based loss that enforces alpha-RGB consistency. Extensive experiments show SSMatte outperforms prior weakly-supervised methods, matches the performance of fully-supervised models on portrait benchmarks, and demonstrates favorable scaling and generalization behaviors with additional data. Our work pushes automatic matting to an fresh, fully annotation-free paradigm. Code will be available.

AI.tldr: SSMatte is the first self-supervised framework for automatic image matting that achieves fully-supervised-level performance using only RGB images without any manual annotations, by decomposing the problem into semantic anchoring (via frozen self-supervised ViT features with a Rayleigh-quotient-based loss) and detail matting (via a fixed-point-based alpha-RGB consistency loss).
AI.motivation: High-quality alpha mattes are expensive to annotate, creating a data bottleneck. Prior methods reduce annotation cost with trimaps/masks but still rely on costly per-pixel supervision, limiting scalability and generalization. The authors ask whether automatic matting can be trained using only RGB images with zero manual annotation.
AI.method: SSMatte decomposes matting into (1) semantic anchoring: generates a semantic matting prompt from frozen self-supervised ViT features by propagating class-token seeds via a novel semantic anchoring loss based on a generalized Rayleigh quotient, and (2) detail matting: a network optimized via a fixed-point-based loss that enforces alpha-RGB consistency.
AI.result: SSMatte outperforms prior weakly-supervised methods, matches fully-supervised models on portrait benchmarks, and shows favorable scaling and generalization with additional data.
AI.conclusion: This work pushes automatic matting to a fully annotation-free paradigm, demonstrating that self-supervised learning can rival fully-supervised performance in image matting.

title: CRiT-QA: Evaluating Multi-hop Reasoning with Counterfactual Chains and Distractor Traps
summary: Evaluating the multi-hop reasoning capabilities of large language models remains a significant challenge. Although current models achieve strong results on existing multi-hop question answering datasets, such performance often masks two critical vulnerabilities: (1) reliance on internal parametric knowledge rather than adherence to the provided context, and (2) exploitation of dataset shortcuts, such as single-document cues or type-matching, that diminish the need for genuine evidence aggregation across multiple documents. We introduce CRiT-QA (Counterfactual Reasoning with Traps), a dataset explicitly designed to address both limitations. To neutralize reliance on memorized knowledge and enforce strict context dependency, CRiT-QA transforms factual reasoning chains with counterfactual entities. Furthermore, it injects multi-anchor distractor chains, plausible but incorrect reasoning paths that diverge at different hops. These traps require models to follow the entire reasoning process rather than exploiting shallow heuristics. Our experiments show that LLMs exhibit substantial performance degradation on CRiT-QA compared to standard datasets, exposing their vulnerability to counterfactual conditions and distractor traps. CRiT-QA thus serves as a rigorous diagnostic tool for evaluating genuine multi-hop reasoning and provides a foundation for developing more reliable, evidence-grounded LLMs.

AI.tldr: CRiT-QA is a counterfactual multi-hop QA dataset with distractor traps that exposes LLMs' reliance on parametric knowledge and shortcut exploitation, causing substantial performance degradation compared to standard datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-hop QA datasets fail to reveal two critical LLM vulnerabilities: reliance on internal parametric knowledge over provided context, and exploitation of dataset shortcuts (e.g., single-document cues, type-matching) that bypass genuine multi-document evidence aggregation.
AI.method: CRiT-QA transforms factual reasoning chains with counterfactual entities to neutralize memorized knowledge, and injects multi-anchor distractor chains (plausible but incorrect reasoning paths diverging at different hops) to force models to follow the full reasoning process rather than exploiting shallow heuristics.
AI.result: LLMs exhibit substantial performance degradation on CRiT-QA compared to standard datasets, exposing their vulnerability to counterfactual conditions and distractor traps.
AI.conclusion: CRiT-QA serves as a rigorous diagnostic tool for evaluating genuine multi-hop reasoning and provides a foundation for developing more reliable, evidence-grounded LLMs.

title: The Differential Neural Tangent Kernel and Its Positivity
summary: The Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) is one powerful tool for analyzing the training dynamics of neural networks in the over-parameterized regime. Recently, the theoretical framework has been extended to physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for solving linear PDEs, one highly popular class of neural PDE solvers. In the analysis, the positivity of the associated NTK plays a fundamental role. However, establishing the positivity of the NTK for PINNs is highly challenging, due to the presence of multiple differential operators. In this work, we propose a new theoretical framework, called Differential Neural Tangent Kernel (DNTK), for analyzing PINNs through the lens of the NTK, and establish the positivity of the infinite width DNTK for both shallow and deep neural networks for a wide class of activation functions, including RePU and smooth but non-polynomial activations, for all linear differential operators. These theoretical results lay the foundation for the analysis of gradient type algorithms for training PINNs.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Differential Neural Tangent Kernel (DNTK) framework to analyze physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for solving linear PDEs. It establishes the positivity of the infinite-width DNTK for shallow and deep networks with various activation functions (RePU, smooth non-polynomial) across all linear differential operators, addressing a key challenge in prior NTK-based PINN analysis.
AI.motivation: While the NTK has been successfully used to analyze standard neural networks, extending this framework to PINNs is challenging due to multiple differential operators involved in the loss function. The positivity of the associated kernel—a fundamental requirement for analyzing training dynamics—is difficult to establish in the PINN setting.
AI.method: The authors propose the Differential Neural Tangent Kernel (DNTK) framework, a theoretical extension of the NTK tailored to PINNs. They prove the positivity of the infinite-width DNTK for both shallow and deep neural networks, covering a wide class of activation functions (e.g., RePU, smooth non-polynomial activations) and all linear differential operators.
AI.result: The infinite-width DNTK is proven to be positive for shallow and deep networks with RePU and smooth non-polynomial activations, for any linear differential operator. This resolves the key theoretical challenge of kernel positivity in NTK-based analysis of PINNs.
AI.conclusion: The established positivity results provide the theoretical foundation for analyzing gradient-based training algorithms for PINNs, enabling future work on convergence guarantees and training dynamics in the neural PDE solver setting.

title: SynthDocBench: Controlled Benchmark for Long-Context Visual Document Understanding
comment: 29 Pages, 27 Tables, 13 Figures, Accepted at COLM 2026
summary: Vision language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on visual document understanding benchmarks such as DocVQA, ChartQA, and MMLongBench-Doc. However, real-world documents combine multiple factors such as length, layout complexity, modality, and question difficulty, which makes it difficult to attribute model failures to specific causes. We introduce SynthDocBench, a fully synthetic benchmark for long-context visual document understanding that systematically controls factors including document length, layout structure, modality composition, and question type. The benchmark is constructed using a combinatorial design, each factor is varied independently across generated documents, enabling controlled analysis of model behavior. Documents are generated end to end using an LLM pipeline across six layout archetypes, with a 40 percent random override to prevent models from exploiting spurious correlations. Additionally, SynthDocBench spans long-context documents with substantially greater length and structural diversity than existing benchmarks. Evaluating seven frontier VLMs, we uncover three failure modes that existing benchmarks cannot surface: sharp degradation with document length, a systematic positional sensitivity in which the middle third of a document is hardest for five of six models and five of six models show a negative Early-to-Late trend (steepest decline: 8.3 percentage points), and breakdown of chart comprehension in long-document settings. These results suggest that current models may be overfitting to benchmark artifacts rather than achieving robust long-context visual document understanding.

AI.tldr: SynthDocBench is a fully synthetic, combinatorially designed benchmark for long-context visual document understanding that controls for document length, layout, modality, and question type. Evaluating seven VLMs reveals three failure modes unseen in existing benchmarks: performance degradation with length, positional sensitivity (middle-third hardest), and chart comprehension breakdown in long documents, suggesting overfitting to benchmark artifacts.
AI.motivation: Existing VLM benchmarks (DocVQA, ChartQA, MMLongBench-Doc) conflate multiple factors (length, layout, modality, difficulty), making it impossible to attribute model failures to specific causes. The authors aim to systematically isolate these factors to uncover fundamental robustness issues.
AI.method: Combinatorial design with independent variation of document length, layout structure, modality composition, and question type across six layout archetypes, using an LLM-based end-to-end generation pipeline with a 40% random override to prevent spurious correlations. Documents are significantly longer and more structurally diverse than existing benchmarks.
AI.result: Seven frontier VLMs evaluated. Three failure modes identified: (1) sharp degradation with document length, (2) systematic positional sensitivity (middle third of document hardest for 5/6 models), and (3) breakdown of chart comprehension in long-document settings. Five of six models show a negative Early-to-Late trend (steepest decline: 8.3 percentage points).
AI.conclusion: Current VLMs may be overfitting to benchmark artifacts rather than achieving robust long-context visual document understanding, as evidenced by failure modes that existing benchmarks cannot surface.

title: Laguerre Geometry for Interpreting Large Language Models
summary: Existing hypotheses represent a concept in an LLM as a single point, a linear direction, or a Gaussian cluster, yet it remains unclear how and why such structures emerge. Here, we show that concept geometry can be precisely characterized via Laguerre Geometry, in which a concept is defined as a region--a Laguerre-Voronoi cell or a union of cells--allowing us to strictly define, measure, and separate concepts. Building on this formulation, we show that finer-grained concept structures, such as inclusion and hierarchy, are naturally revealed by the Laguerre weights. We then push this geometry inside the transformer. Decomposing each layer into piecewise-linear operators, we show that a token's hidden trajectory is governed by two coupled mechanisms: a static tree of self-contained piecewise-linear flow, and a dynamic transport that hops the trajectory across trees when cross-token attention fires. This decomposition yields Geometric Lens, a training-free, hyperparameter-free method for reading out the exact concept a hidden vector encodes at any layer. We also develop Laguerre Autoencoder, a 2D visualizer that renders both the decision geometry and a model's full reasoning trajectory in one view. Finally, we move beyond explanatory geometry toward actionable interpretability, showing that Geometric Lens recovers the correct factual token when a model is prompted with in-context interference. The code is available on GitHub.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Laguerre Geometry to characterize concept representations in LLMs as regions (Laguerre-Voronoi cells) rather than points or directions, introduces Geometric Lens for training-free concept decoding from hidden states, and develops a Laguerre Autoencoder for 2D visualization of reasoning trajectories, with applications to interpretability and factual recovery under in-context interference.
AI.motivation: Existing concept representation models (points, linear directions, Gaussian clusters) lack a precise framework to explain how and why concept structures emerge in LLMs, motivating the need for a more rigorous geometric characterization.
AI.method: (1) Formulates concept geometry via Laguerre Geometry, defining concepts as Laguerre-Voronoi cells or unions thereof; (2) Decomposes transformer layers into piecewise-linear operators, revealing a static tree of piecewise-linear flow and dynamic cross-token attention transport; (3) Introduces Geometric Lens (training-free, hyperparameter-free) to decode exact concepts from hidden vectors; (4) Develops Laguerre Autoencoder for 2D visualization of decision geometry and reasoning trajectories.
AI.result: Geometric Lens recovers correct factual tokens under in-context interference, demonstrating actionable interpretability beyond explanatory analysis.
AI.conclusion: Laguerre Geometry provides a precise, unified framework for understanding concept structures (including inclusion and hierarchy) in LLMs, and enables practical interpretability tools without additional training.

title: Two Confounds in Cross-Model Value Comparison: Response Determinism and the Access Harness
summary: Cross-model comparisons read divergence in value dispositions as evidence that language models hold individuated values. Under single-draw measurement this conflates two quantities: a difference in central tendency (a genuine value difference) and a difference in response determinism (how sharply a model commits to a forced choice). We introduce a separation protocol -- no-rule value dilemmas with counterbalanced, repeated forced-choice measurement and a determinism index -- and a determinism-corrected decomposition that splits an apparent cross-model distance into a direction-flip component (genuine disagreement) and a same-side-more-extreme component we label determinism. Across nine models, determinism varies substantially (0.66-0.95 among engaging models); whether it is a per-model trait or tracks provider and scale is a question our method makes measurable but our sample leaves open. Correcting for determinism shrinks apparent individuation, while a few cross-family disagreements survive a strict test. We then isolate a second confound: the access harness serving each model. Re-collecting the same models through raw provider APIs, we find the deployment client shifts a model's value profile substantially and client-specifically: one subscription CLI moves a profile by 0.31, flips four of eighteen items, and inflates the flagship's apparent softness (0.34 via CLI vs 0.66 via raw API), whereas another provider's client is clean, confounding provider family with access client. The harness is a value-shaping layer: a base model that refuses one-in-ten forced choices is made compliant by an agent system prompt, established causally in a white-box control. An audit ranking models by single-draw value distance thus ranks a determinism-inflated quantity, confounded further by the client used. We contribute the decomposition and identify the deployment harness as a distinct value confound.

AI.tldr: Cross-model comparisons of value dispositions conflate genuine value differences with response determinism and deployment harness effects. We introduce a separation protocol and determinism-corrected decomposition, finding determinism varies substantially across models (0.66-0.95) and the access client shifts value profiles substantially, making the deployment harness a distinct value confound.
AI.motivation: Current cross-model value comparisons under single-draw measurement conflate two distinct quantities: genuine value differences (central tendency) and response determinism (how sharply a model commits to a forced choice), motivating the need for a separation protocol.
AI.method: No-rule value dilemmas with counterbalanced, repeated forced-choice measurement and a determinism index; determinism-corrected decomposition splitting apparent cross-model distance into direction-flip (genuine disagreement) and same-side-more-extreme (determinism) components; additional collection through raw provider APIs to isolate access harness effects.
AI.result: Determinism varies from 0.66-0.95 among engaging models; client-specific shifts in value profiles (one CLI moves profile by 0.31, flips four of eighteen items); base model made compliant by agent system prompt, established causally.
AI.conclusion: The deployment harness is a distinct value confound; auditing models by single-draw value distance ranks a determinism-inflated quantity confounded further by the client used. The decomposition and identification of deployment harness as a confound are the contributions.

title: TVT-PAPD: Pathology-Aware Prototype Distillation for Self-Supervised Whole Slide Image Classification
summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as an effective paradigm for learning transferable representations from large-scale unlabeled whole slide images (WSIs). However, existing SSL methods primarily learn generic visual features and often fail to explicitly capture pathology-specific morphological patterns that are critical for disease characterization. To address this limitation, we propose Tiny Vision Transformer with Pathology-Aware Prototype Distillation (TVT-PAPD). This self-supervised pathology representation learning framework integrates a Tiny Vision Transformer (TVT) with a novel Pathology-Aware Prototype Distillation (PAPD) module. PAPD employs a learnable pathology prototype bank to discover and preserve representative tissue morphology patterns, encouraging semantically similar pathological regions to learn consistent and discriminative representations. The proposed framework enhances pathology-aware feature learning while maintaining computational efficiency with 90M parameters. Experiments on the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) low-grade glioma (LGG)/glioblastoma (GBM) dataset and the Indian Pathology Brain (IPD-Brain) dataset demonstrate that TVT-PAPD achieves weighted F1-scores of 93.02% and 90.23%, respectively, for LGG-GBM classification, while exhibiting strong cross-cohort generalization across independent glioma datasets.

AI.tldr: TVT-PAPD integrates a Tiny Vision Transformer with Pathology-Aware Prototype Distillation to learn pathology-specific morphological patterns from unlabeled whole slide images, achieving weighted F1-scores of 93.02% (TCGA) and 90.23% (IPD-Brain) for LGG-GBM classification with 90M parameters.
AI.motivation: Existing SSL methods for WSIs learn generic visual features but fail to explicitly capture pathology-specific morphological patterns critical for disease characterization.
AI.method: Proposes TVT-PAPD, combining a Tiny Vision Transformer (TVT) with a Pathology-Aware Prototype Distillation (PAPD) module that uses a learnable pathology prototype bank to discover and preserve representative tissue morphology patterns, enforcing consistent and discriminative representations for semantically similar pathological regions.
AI.result: Weighted F1-scores of 93.02% on TCGA LGG/GBM and 90.23% on IPD-Brain datasets for glioma classification, with strong cross-cohort generalization across independent glioma datasets, using only 90M parameters.
AI.conclusion: TVT-PAPD effectively enhances pathology-aware feature learning in a computationally efficient manner, outperforming prior SSL approaches on glioma classification and generalization tasks.

title: Constraint-Aware Hierarchical Search for Regulation-Driven Fine-Grained Classification
summary: Tasks such as customs tariff classification, export control categorization, and standards-based equipment coding require assigning an input instance to a fine-grained class under an explicit regulatory hierarchy. Unlike standard text classification, the correct label in these tasks is not determined by semantic similarity alone, but by rule-defined boundaries, threshold conditions, exclusion clauses, definitions, and local exceptions. As a result, two highly similar inputs may require different labels, while a retrieved passage that appears relevant may still be inapplicable under the governing rules. Existing flat classifiers, hierarchical text classification methods, and retrieval-augmented LLM systems are not designed to jointly enforce hierarchical validity, rule consistency, and fine-grained boundary reasoning. In this paper, we formulate this setting as regulation-driven fine-grained hierarchical classification, where an external instance must be assigned to a fine-grained class through a valid path in a regulatory hierarchy and supported by auditable evidence. We construct four benchmark datasets from representative regulation-intensive scenarios and validate the annotations through an expert-in-the-loop process. We further propose a constraint-aware hierarchical search framework that converts regulatory documents into a searchable tree, retrieves only valid local candidate nodes, and uses structured regulatory fields with evidence snippets to guide each next-hop decision. Experiments show that our method achieves the best mean accuracy on all four datasets and provides interpretable decision paths, with the largest gains on cases involving fine-grained neighboring categories and rule-based boundary conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces regulation-driven fine-grained hierarchical classification, a task where instances must be classified under explicit regulatory hierarchies with rule-defined boundaries. The authors construct four benchmark datasets and propose a constraint-aware hierarchical search framework that outperforms existing methods by enforcing hierarchical validity, rule consistency, and providing interpretable decision paths.
AI.motivation: Existing flat classifiers, hierarchical text classification methods, and retrieval-augmented LLM systems cannot jointly enforce hierarchical validity, rule consistency, and fine-grained boundary reasoning required by regulatory tasks (e.g., customs tariff classification, export control categorization), where semantically similar inputs may require different labels due to explicit rules, thresholds, exclusions, and local exceptions.
AI.method: The authors propose a constraint-aware hierarchical search framework that converts regulatory documents into a searchable tree, retrieves only valid local candidate nodes, and uses structured regulatory fields with evidence snippets to guide each next-hop decision. They also construct four benchmark datasets from regulation-intensive scenarios with expert-in-the-loop validation.
AI.result: The proposed method achieves the best mean accuracy on all four datasets, with the largest gains on cases involving fine-grained neighboring categories and rule-based boundary conditions, while providing interpretable decision paths.
AI.conclusion: The proposed constraint-aware hierarchical search framework effectively addresses regulation-driven fine-grained hierarchical classification by enforcing rule consistency and hierarchical validity, outperforming existing methods across four diverse regulatory scenarios.

title: When Does Depth Survive Composition? Compute--Quality Regimes in Latent World Models
summary: Adaptive-compute world models -- early-exit or mixture-of-depths predictors that spend variable depth per step -- assume depth buys better predictions and can be routed adaptively. In autoregressive rollouts, the first assumption requires depth's per-step precision to survive composition. We test this with a pre-registered instrument, the shallow penalty $ρ=\mathrm{err}(\text{shallowest-exit rollout})/\mathrm{err}(\text{full-depth rollout})$, across nine DeepMind Control tasks under matched single-step ($K=1$) and multi-step ($K=4$) training, three seeds each. We find three regimes: on 6/9 tasks depth helps rollouts (intrinsic, $ρ$ up to $4.7\times$), on 2/9 the shallow exits beat the full stack (inversion, $ρ$ down to $0.85\times$), and one is flat. The robust inversion (cheetah) is not a property of the dynamics but is created by training: an ablation supervising early exits only at the first rollout step erases it ($ρ: 0.87\to1.18$, $n=8$, $Δ=+0.31$), while an intrinsic-tradeoff task is unaffected -- a double dissociation we call the routability catch-22, since the supervision that makes exits routable is what trains them to out-roll the full stack. The regime is partly predictable a priori: observation/action dimensionality and one-step model error correlate with $ρ$ at $|\text{Spearman}|\approx0.75$ ($n=9$). Inside a CEM planner, $ρ$'s sign predicts whether planning benefits from depth, most sharply on the inversion task, where shallow planning beats deep. Finally, three cautions: a task's regime depends on the metric space, the rollout horizon, and the encoder. All thresholds and gates were fixed before the compute campaign, including a pre-registered negative for the hypothesis that motivated the study.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates whether adaptive-compute world models (early-exit or mixture-of-depths predictors) actually benefit from spending more depth per step in autoregressive rollouts. Across 9 DeepMind Control tasks, they find three regimes: depth helps (6/9), depth hurts/inversion (2/9), or flat (1/9). The inversion is caused by training supervision, creating a "routability catch-22" where making exits routable trains them to outperform the full stack. Regime is partly predictable from observation/action dimensionality and one-step error.
AI.motivation: To test the assumption that spending more depth per step in adaptive-compute world models improves prediction accuracy when composed autoregressively over multiple rollout steps.
AI.method: Pre-registered study using a shallow penalty metric ρ = err(shallowest-exit rollout)/err(full-depth rollout) across 9 DeepMind Control tasks, comparing single-step (K=1) and multi-step (K=4) training with 3 seeds each. Includes ablation studies, CEM planning analysis, and correlation analysis with task properties.
AI.result: Three regimes identified: intrinsic (depth helps, ρ up to 4.7× on 6/9 tasks), inversion (shallow exits beat full stack, ρ down to 0.85× on 2/9), and flat (1/9). Inversion is caused by training supervision - ablating early-exit supervision at first rollout step erases it (ρ: 0.87→1.18). Observation/action dimensionality and one-step error correlate with ρ at |Spearman|≈0.75.
AI.conclusion: The routability catch-22: the supervision that makes exits routable is what trains them to outperform the full stack. ρ's sign predicts whether CEM planning benefits from depth. Regime depends on metric space, rollout horizon, and encoder.

title: GNOCHI: Generative Neural mOdel for Close Human-Human Interactions
summary: Creating realistic 3D human-human interactions in virtual environments is challenging due to the high degrees of freedom in the human body and the need for physically accurate poses that do not collide with each other. Traditional methods for human-human interaction are based on motion tracking or 3D body reconstruction, but lack generative capabilities. Recent generative methods enable the synthesis of individual or interacting motions via text or image input, but generally fall short in modeling close interactions. This paper introduces a novel generative model for close 3D human-human interactions using a conditional variational autoencoder (cVAE), which generates poses for one human conditioned on the pose of another, allowing for controlled and diverse interaction synthesis. To train our model, we address two underlying long-standing challenges in the field of human-human interaction: data scarcity, for which we propose an automated supervised data augmentation strategy that generates synthetic yet realistic interaction poses; and collision awareness in generative approaches, for which we propose a self-supervised loss based on a collision resolution technique using volumetric proxies to ensure physically correct interactions. We extensively evaluate the capabilities of our model, and demonstrate a wide variety of plausible and physically correct interactions, not possible to generate with current state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: A novel cVAE-based generative model for close 3D human-human interactions that generates poses conditioned on a partner's pose, using supervised data augmentation to address data scarcity and a self-supervised collision loss with volumetric proxies to ensure physically correct, collision-free interactions.
AI.motivation: Creating realistic 3D human-human interactions in virtual environments is challenging due to high body DOFs and the need for physically accurate, non-colliding poses. Existing methods lack generative capabilities or fail to model close interactions effectively.
AI.method: A conditional variational autoencoder (cVAE) that generates poses for one human conditioned on another's pose; an automated supervised data augmentation strategy for synthetic yet realistic interaction poses; and a self-supervised collision loss based on volumetric proxy-based collision resolution for physically correct poses.
AI.result: The model generates a wide variety of plausible and physically correct close interactions that are not possible with current state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed generative model successfully addresses data scarcity and collision awareness in close human-human interaction synthesis, enabling controlled and diverse interaction generation for virtual environments.

title: MRUF: Multi-granularity Routing with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion for Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
comment: Main paper (6 pages). Accepted for publication by IEEE International Conference on Systems and Man and and Cybernetics 2026 (IEEE SMC 2026)
summary: Multimodal sentiment analysis relies on language, visual, and acoustic cues, but utterance-level modality quality may vary due to occlusion, background noise, motion blur, or imperfect transcripts, causing conventional fusion to over-trust unreliable modalities. We propose MRUF, a reliability-aware fusion method that combines multi-granularity routing with uncertainty-aware calibration. MRUF summarizes sentiment-relevant representations, performs subspace- and modality-level routing, and supervises modality routing with leave-one-out error increases to estimate utterance-level modality importance. It further predicts modality-wise uncertainty and refines modality gates through inverse-variance reweighting, while modality-invariant contrastive alignment stabilizes the shared representation space. Experiments on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI under aligned and unaligned settings show consistent improvements over strong baselines, and mechanism analysis verifies that modalities with higher predicted uncertainty receive lower fusion weights.

AI.tldr: MRUF is a reliability-aware multimodal fusion method that uses multi-granularity routing, uncertainty calibration, and modality-invariant contrastive alignment to handle varying utterance-level modality quality, achieving consistent improvements on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI.
AI.motivation: Utterance-level modality quality may vary due to occlusion, background noise, motion blur, or imperfect transcripts, causing conventional fusion to over-trust unreliable modalities.
AI.method: MRUF combines multi-granularity routing (subspace- and modality-level) with uncertainty-aware calibration. It supervises modality routing using leave-one-out error increases, predicts modality-wise uncertainty, refines gates via inverse-variance reweighting, and uses modality-invariant contrastive alignment.
AI.result: Consistent improvements over strong baselines on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI under both aligned and unaligned settings; modalities with higher predicted uncertainty receive lower fusion weights.
AI.conclusion: Reliability-aware fusion with uncertainty calibration effectively mitigates the effect of unreliable modalities in multimodal sentiment analysis.

title: Exploratory Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Forecasting Meteorological Parameters in the Agricultural Sector
summary: Accurate meteorological forecasting is essential for agricultural planning, irrigation management, and environmental decision support. This study conducts a comparative evaluation of recurrent and hybrid deep learning architectures for multivariate forecasting of reference evapotranspiration ($ET_0$), vapour pressure deficit (VPD), wind speed, and the sine and cosine components of wind direction. The analysis utilizes 134,376 hourly observations from Ioannina, Greece, spanning January 2011 to April 2026, sourced from ERA5 via the OpenMeteo Historical Weather API. Single and multi-layer GRU and LSTM networks are compared with hybrid 1D-CNN-GRU and 1D-CNN-LSTM models for two forecasting tasks: a 24-hour next-day forecast and a 168-hour week-ahead forecast. Performance is evaluated using normalized root mean squared error, the coefficient of determination, and a composite Weighted Quotient Score (WQS). The most effective purely recurrent models are a 64-unit LSTM for the 24-hour horizon, with a WQS of 0.816755, and a 1024-unit GRU for the 168-hour horizon, with a WQS of 0.779465. The hybrid CNN-GRU models achieved the highest overall scores of 0.827535 and 0.782863 for the 24-hour and 168-hour horizons, but with additionally more number of units respectively to LSTM models, while the CNN-LSTM models yield nearly identical results with substantially fewer parameters. Compared to the corresponding recurrent baselines, the hybrid models improve WQS by 1.22--1.63\% at 24 hours and by 0.44--0.45\% at 168 hours, indicating that convolutional feature extraction is more beneficial for short-term forecasting.

AI.tldr: This study compares recurrent (GRU, LSTM) and hybrid (1D-CNN-GRU, 1D-CNN-LSTM) deep learning models for multivariate meteorological forecasting (ET₀, VPD, wind components) using 134K hourly observations from Ioannina, Greece. For 24-hour forecasts, a 64-unit LSTM (WQS=0.8168) and CNN-GRU (WQS=0.8275) performed best; for 168-hour forecasts, a 1024-unit GRU (WQS=0.7795) and CNN-GRU (WQS=0.7829) led. Hybrid models improved WQS by 1.22-1.63% (24h) and 0.44-0.45% (168h), with CNN-LSTM offering near-identical results at lower parameter counts.
AI.motivation: Accurate meteorological forecasting is essential for agricultural planning, irrigation management, and environmental decision support, motivating a systematic comparison of deep learning architectures for multivariate evapotranspiration and meteorological variable prediction.
AI.method: Single and multi-layer GRU and LSTM networks were compared with hybrid 1D-CNN-GRU and 1D-CNN-LSTM models for two forecasting tasks (24-hour next-day and 168-hour week-ahead), evaluated using nRMSE, R², and a composite Weighted Quotient Score (WQS) on 134,376 hourly ERA5 observations from Ioannina, Greece.
AI.result: For 24-hour horizon: 64-unit LSTM (WQS=0.816755) and CNN-GRU (WQS=0.827535) were best. For 168-hour horizon: 1024-unit GRU (WQS=0.779465) and CNN-GRU (WQS=0.782863) were best. Hybrid models improved WQS by 1.22-1.63% (24h) and 0.44-0.45% (168h); CNN-LSTM achieved near-identical performance with fewer parameters.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid CNN-recurrent architectures outperform purely recurrent models, with convolutional feature extraction providing greater benefits for short-term (24-hour) forecasting than for week-ahead (168-hour) forecasting. CNN-LSTM offers a favorable parameter efficiency trade-off.

title: SPORT: Structure-Aware Prototype Disentanglement for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering
summary: Prototype-based Incomplete Multi-view Clustering has recently attracted increasing attention by exploiting prototypes as semantic anchors for missing-view imputation. However, existing approaches are still limited in three aspects. First, they typically focus on enforcing cross-view prototype consistency, while ignoring view-specific information embedded in prototypes, thus limiting multi-view expressiveness. Second, most methods rely on instance-level contrastive learning that only aligns paired samples across views, failing to preserve cluster-level relational structures. Third, missing-view imputation is usually performed using global prototypes alone, without considering local geometric neighborhood structures, leading to inaccurate recovery of missing representations. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework termed Structure-aware PrOtotype disentanglement foR incomplete multi-view clusTering (SPORT), which explicitly disentangles shared and view-specific components of prototypes while preserving cluster-level relational structures. Specifically, we decouple prototypes into orthogonal shared and view-specific components, aligning only shared components to capture consensus semantics while de-correlating view-specific components to preserve complementary information. Meanwhile, a structure-aware contrastive learning mechanism is incorporated to explicitly model cluster-level relationships during cross-view representation learning. Furthermore, a hybrid imputation strategy integrates global prototype matching with local neighborhood matching, enabling joint exploitation of semantic prototypes and manifold structures for missing-view recovery. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets show that SPORT achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods under various missing rates.

AI.tldr: SPORT is a novel incomplete multi-view clustering framework that disentangles prototypes into shared and view-specific components, uses structure-aware contrastive learning for cluster-level relations, and employs a hybrid imputation strategy combining global prototype matching with local neighborhood matching, achieving state-of-the-art performance on six benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing prototype-based incomplete multi-view clustering methods suffer from three limitations: (1) ignoring view-specific prototype information, (2) relying on instance-level rather than cluster-level contrastive learning, and (3) using only global prototypes for missing-view imputation without considering local geometric structures.
AI.method: (1) Decouples prototypes into orthogonal shared and view-specific components, aligning shared components for consensus semantics while de-correlating view-specific components for complementary info; (2) Structure-aware contrastive learning to model cluster-level relationships; (3) Hybrid imputation strategy combining global prototype matching with local neighborhood matching.
AI.result: Superior performance over state-of-the-art methods across six benchmark datasets under various missing rates.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly disentangling shared and view-specific prototype components while preserving cluster-level structures and leveraging both global and local information for imputation effectively addresses key limitations in incomplete multi-view clustering.

title: Agentic-DPO: From Imitation to Agentic Policy Optimization on Expert Trajectories
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are commonly trained from expert trajectories using supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which treats multi-turn agent behavior as ordinary text imitation. This recipe is simple and low-cost, but it only learns to imitate the sequence of expert actions, rather than training the agent to choose the right action against plausible mistakes at each state. Existing methods to mitigate this problem include preference learning or reinforcement learning, but they usually need high-cost environment rollouts and reward models. We propose Agentic-DPO, a lightweight offline agent policy optimization method that turns expert trajectories into state-conditioned preference supervision. At each expert action state, Agentic-DPO samples a one-step action from the current state, treats plausible wrong actions as negatives, and contrasts them with the expert action using a DPO-style preference objective. To avoid mixing both policy and schema in preference learning, we introduce Policy-Preserving Augmentation (PPA), which renders the same latent trajectory under multiple schemas while keeping the expert policy fixed. Agentic-DPO requires no online environment rollout, reward model, or full-trajectory student exploration. We conduct experiments across StableToolBench, tau-bench retail, and Mind2Web, where Agentic-DPO consistently improves agents at different model scales beyond imitation. In particular, it raises tau-bench accuracy from 21.7% (SFT) to 41.4% for a 9B model, matching online GRPO under the same backbone with only step-level rollouts and without environment interaction during gradient steps. The results suggest that expert trajectories can support low-cost agentic policy optimization when converted from demonstrations into state-level action preferences. Code for Agentic-DPO is released at https://github.com/Schuture/Agentic-DPO.

AI.tldr: Agentic-DPO is a lightweight offline method for optimizing LLM agent policies by converting expert trajectories into state-conditioned preference supervision using DPO-style objectives with Policy-Preserving Augmentation (PPA), achieving significant improvements over SFT without requiring online rollouts, reward models, or full-trajectory exploration.
AI.motivation: SFT on expert trajectories only learns to imitate sequences of actions rather than training agents to choose correct actions against plausible mistakes at each state. Existing solutions (preference learning, RL) require costly environment rollouts and reward models.
AI.method: Agentic-DPO: (1) samples one-step actions from the current state, treats plausible wrong actions as negatives, and contrasts them with expert actions using a DPO-style preference objective; (2) introduces Policy-Preserving Augmentation (PPA) to render the same latent trajectory under multiple schemas while keeping the expert policy fixed, avoiding conflating policy and schema in preference learning.
AI.result: Consistently improves agent performance across StableToolBench, tau-bench retail, and Mind2Web. Raises tau-bench accuracy from 21.7% (SFT) to 41.4% for a 9B model, matching online GRPO with only step-level rollouts and no environment interaction during gradient steps.
AI.conclusion: Expert trajectories can support low-cost agentic policy optimization when converted from demonstrations into state-level action preferences, eliminating the need for online rollouts, reward models, or full-trajectory student exploration.

title: DSSMs: State Space Models with Explicit Memory via Delay Differential Equations
summary: State Space Models (SSMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for efficient long-sequence modeling, offering parallel training and fast linear-time recurrent inference. However, like other recurrent architectures, SSMs must compress an unbounded history into a fixed-size state, which limits context retention and makes precise retrieval over long-range context inherently difficult. To overcome this limitation, we propose Delay State Space Models (DSSMs), a delay differential equation (DDE)-inspired extension of diagonal SSMs that augments discrete SSM recurrences with explicit delayed-state feedback. Making explicit delayed feedback practical requires new stability parameterization, history management, and FFT-training tools. We address these challenges with a practical discretization and parameterization grounded in a simple delay-independent stability condition. To bypass direct time-domain kernel construction, we derive the DSSM transfer function and compute kernels in the frequency domain, using a kernel contour shift to suppress aliasing and recover accurate FFT training. Empirically, DSSMs substantially improve targeted delayed-retrieval tasks while outperforming S4D on most standard sequence metrics and remaining close on the others.

AI.tldr: DSSMs extend diagonal SSMs with explicit delayed-state feedback via delay differential equations, enabling improved long-range context retention and retrieval while maintaining efficient FFT-based training.
AI.motivation: SSMs compress unbounded history into fixed-size states, limiting context retention and making precise long-range retrieval inherently difficult. The authors propose DSSMs to overcome this limitation.
AI.method: DSSMs augment discrete SSM recurrences with explicit delayed-state feedback, grounded in delay differential equations. They introduce a delay-independent stability condition, a practical discretization/parameterization, frequency-domain kernel computation via transfer function, and a kernel contour shift to suppress aliasing for accurate FFT training.
AI.result: DSSMs substantially improve targeted delayed-retrieval tasks, outperform S4D on most standard sequence metrics, and remain competitive on the remaining ones.
AI.conclusion: Explicit delayed-state feedback is a viable and effective enhancement to diagonal SSMs for improving long-range context retention without sacrificing training efficiency.

title: BOCCHI: A More Realistic and Challenging Benchmark for Local Motion Blur Detection with MSDCT-UNet
summary: Local motion blur detection requires pixel-level localization of blurred regions. Existing benchmarks let models rely on gradient shortcuts that fail to transfer. We introduce BOCCHI (Blurred Objects Captured across Cameras with Human-annotated Imagery), a real-captured benchmark whose sharp regions overlap the blur gradient distribution and defeat these shortcuts, and propose MSDCT-UNet (Multi-Scale Discrete Cosine Transform UNet), a frequency-aware encoder-decoder injecting multi-scale DCT priors through DCT Attention and FiLM. MSDCT-UNet ranks first in in-domain mIoU and boundary localization on BOCCHI, and BOCCHI-trained models outperform every other training source on cross-dataset transfer with only 633 training images.

AI.tldr: Introduces BOCCHI (real-captured blur detection benchmark) and MSDCT-UNet (frequency-aware network with multi-scale DCT priors), achieving state-of-the-art in-domain and cross-dataset performance.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks let models rely on gradient shortcuts (distribution gaps between sharp/blur regions) that fail to transfer to real-world scenarios, motivating a benchmark that eliminates these shortcuts.
AI.method: BOCCHI: real-captured dataset where sharp regions overlap blur gradient distribution. MSDCT-UNet: encoder-decoder injecting multi-scale DCT priors via DCT Attention and FiLM modules for frequency-aware blur detection.
AI.result: MSDCT-UNet achieves #1 in-domain mIoU and boundary localization on BOCCHI; BOCCHI-trained models outperform all other training sources on cross-dataset transfer using only 633 training images.
AI.conclusion: BOCCHI defeats gradient shortcuts and enables better generalization; MSDCT-UNet's frequency-aware design is effective for local motion blur detection.

title: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
summary: Memory is becoming a core component of long-horizon AI agents, allowing agents to reuse past experience when operating web browsers, software tools, and other interactive environments. Existing work mostly treats memory as a supply problem, asking what experience to write, how to store it, and which entry to retrieve for the next task. Yet we still lack a clear account of how models consume retrieved memory across a multi-step action trajectory. This consumption process matters because it determines not only what memories should be retrieved, but also what models and control policies are needed to use them safely. To diagnose this process, we propose Entry--Propagation--Recovery (E-P-R), a trajectory-level framework that asks where memory first changes an action, whether that change carries forward, and whether the agent can recover after leaving a correct path. We instantiate E-P-R on WebArena and on MemTrapBench, a controlled benchmark we build to isolate these phases. We find that the main failure often begins at entry: agents adopt conflicting memory at the first exposed decision point even when it is task-wrong. Repeated exposure then amplifies this early error, while recovery after divergence is weak. Together, these effects create a compliance trap: across models, conflicting memory induces similar compliance rates, but once agents comply, their success rates collapse to a low floor. Stronger agents therefore suffer larger absolute damage because each compliance event erases more baseline capability. These results suggest that memory-augmented agents should be evaluated not only by retrieval quality or final success rate, but by how they consume memory throughout the trajectory.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes E-P-R (Entry-Propagation-Recovery), a trajectory-level framework for diagnosing how AI agents consume retrieved memory across multi-step actions. Experiments on WebArena and a new MemTrapBench benchmark reveal a "compliance trap": conflicting memory causes early errors that amplify over time with weak recovery, and while all models show similar compliance rates, stronger agents suffer greater absolute performance drops due to more baseline capability loss per compliance event.
AI.motivation: Existing work treats memory as a supply problem (what to store and retrieve), but lacks a clear understanding of how models consume retrieved memory across multi-step action trajectories, which is critical for determining what memories to retrieve and what control policies are needed for safe usage.
AI.method: The authors propose E-P-R (Entry-Propagation-Recovery), a trajectory-level framework with three phases: (1) Entry - where memory first changes an action, (2) Propagation - whether that change carries forward, (3) Recovery - whether the agent can recover after leaving a correct path. The framework is instantiated on WebArena and a new controlled benchmark, MemTrapBench, designed to isolate these phases.
AI.result: The main failure begins at entry: agents adopt conflicting memory at the first exposed decision point even when task-wrong. Repeated exposure amplifies early errors, while recovery after divergence is weak. A "compliance trap" emerges: across models, conflicting memory induces similar compliance rates, but once agents comply, success rates collapse to a low floor. Stronger agents suffer larger absolute damage because each compliance event erases more baseline capability.
AI.conclusion: Memory-augmented agents should be evaluated not only by retrieval quality or final success rate, but by how they consume memory throughout the trajectory, with attention to the entry-propagation-recovery dynamics.

title: Data-Driven Telecom Marketing Optimization: A Machine Learning-Based Churn Prediction and Customer Segmentation Framework
summary: Customer churn is a major challenge for telecommunication companies, directly eroding revenue and long term customer relationships. Traditional retention programs rely on generic, not personalized incentives and lack the precision to identify high risk customers before they leave. This paper presents a data driven marketing optimization framework integrating machine learning based churn prediction, customer segmentation combining churn risk with customer value, and tailored, segment specific marketing and Return on Investment ROI strategies. Using the IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset with 7043 customers and 21 features, three gradient boosting ensembles, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, were trained and tuned via randomized search with stratified 5 fold cross validation, class weighting, and F1 score driven decision threshold optimization to counter a class imbalance of 73.4% versus 26.6%. CatBoost was selected as the deployment model, achieving 77.68% accuracy, an F1 score of 0.6366, a PR AUC of 0.6553, and a ROC AUC of 0.8403 on the held out test set. Customers were partitioned with K Means clustering, validated via the Elbow method and visualized with Principal Component Analysis, into High, Medium, and Low Value segments, cross tabulated against churn risk labels to define four actionable clusters. Segment specific retention, upsell, and engagement strategies were designed for each cluster, and a theoretical ROI and CLV framework quantifies the financial impact of the proposed interventions. The pipeline was operationalized in an interactive Streamlit web application allowing marketing teams to upload data, filter by segment, visualize churn drivers via SHAP, and download automated segment reports. Results confirm that combining predictive churn modeling with value aware segmentation yields more actionable and profitable marketing decisions than churn prediction alone.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a data-driven marketing optimization framework that integrates CatBoost-based churn prediction, K-Means customer segmentation (High/Medium/Low value), and segment-specific retention/upsell strategies, operationalized via a Streamlit web app, achieving 77.68% accuracy and 0.8403 ROC AUC on the IBM Telco dataset.
AI.motivation: Customer churn directly erodes revenue and long-term relationships for telecom companies, but traditional retention programs use generic incentives and lack the ability to identify high-risk customers before they leave.
AI.method: Three gradient boosting ensembles (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) were trained with randomized search, stratified 5-fold CV, class weighting, and F1-driven threshold optimization. CatBoost was selected (77.68% accuracy, 0.6366 F1, 0.8403 ROC AUC). Customers were partitioned via K-Means (Elbow method, PCA visualization) into High/Medium/Low value segments, cross-tabulated with churn risk to define four actionable clusters. Segment-specific strategies and ROI/CLV frameworks were designed; the pipeline was deployed via Streamlit.
AI.result: CatBoost achieved 77.68% accuracy, F1=0.6366, PR AUC=0.6553, ROC AUC=0.8403 on the held-out test set. Customer segmentation produced four actionable clusters. The integrated framework yields more actionable and profitable marketing decisions than churn prediction alone.
AI.conclusion: Combining predictive churn modeling with value-aware segmentation enables more precise, personalized retention strategies and quantifiable financial impact, outperforming churn-prediction-only approaches for telecom marketing.

title: Annotation-Free Furniture Codes: What They Encode, and How Far They Transfer
summary: Layout-based 3D scene synthesizers place each object using two human-annotated channels: a categorical class label and a canonical-pose convention. We ask whether a single self-supervised token derived from object geometry can replace both, and study such tokens directly as a representation, decoupled from any synthesizer. A Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ) point-cloud autoencoder is chamfer-trained on placed 3D-FUTURE furniture with no labels or pose annotations. Diagnostic probes recover fine-category (62.6 +/- 0.5%), super-category (85.6 +/- 1.3%), and yaw (52.7 +/- 0.5 deg) from the codes alone. Swapping the chamfer target from the rotated to the un-rotated point cloud collapses the yaw signal while raising class recovery, showing the codes' rotation content can be set by the training objective. Scaling across asset libraries needs codes that transfer; on an unseen dataset (ShapeNet), alignment is category-dependent: box-like furniture transfers, organically-shaped furniture does not, and a target-blind augmentation partly closes the gap.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes replacing categorical class labels and canonical-pose conventions with a single self-supervised token derived from object geometry for layout-based 3D scene synthesis. Using a Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ) point-cloud autoencoder trained on 3D-FUTURE furniture without labels, the learned codes recover fine-category (62.6%), super-category (85.6%), and yaw (52.7 deg). Training objective controls rotation content, and cross-dataset transfer depends on shape category.
AI.motivation: To eliminate the need for two separate human-annotated channels (class labels and pose conventions) in layout-based 3D scene synthesis by replacing them with a single self-supervised token derived from object geometry.
AI.method: An FSQ point-cloud autoencoder is trained with a chamfer loss on placed 3D-FUTURE furniture without any labels or pose annotations. Diagnostic probes evaluate category and yaw recovery. Ablation changes chamfer target from rotated to un-rotated point clouds. Cross-dataset transfer is tested on ShapeNet.
AI.result: Codes recover fine-category (62.6±0.5%), super-category (85.6±1.3%), and yaw (52.7±0.5 deg). Rotating chamfer target collapses yaw signal while improving class recovery. Cross-dataset transfer is category-dependent: box-like furniture transfers well, organic shapes do not.
AI.conclusion: A single self-supervised token from geometry can replace both class labels and pose conventions, with rotation content controllable by training objective. Transfer across datasets remains challenging for non-rigid/organic shapes.

title: Embark Now: User Demand Oriented Framework for Multi-day Urban Travel Itinerary Planning
summary: In large urban areas, planning multi-day travel itineraries is challenging due to the abundance of Points of Interest (POIs), diverse user preferences, and constraints such as opening hours. Effective solutions must dynamically accommodate diverse traveler requirements while optimizing for satisfaction and feasibility within limited computation time. This paper addresses these challenges through introducing an innovative framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) to dynamically capture user requirements with precision and flexibility, and an enhanced Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure (GRASP) algorithm as a well-suited preference-aware planner to generate feasible multi-day itineraries. The effectiveness of our integrated approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on two real-world urban datasets from Beijing and Tianjin. Our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, improving the average total itinerary score by at least 4.52% and 11.09% across 5,040 user cases with diverse preferences in the two datasets. Furthermore, through end-to-end algorithmic enhancements, it achieves notable average improvements of 17.95% and 26.07% in the computed metrics, while also delivering substantial gains in time efficiency -- realizing average performance increases of 4.64% and 25.55% within shorter computation times compared to suboptimal methods that require multiple iterations. These outcomes underscore our method's superiority in delivering both enhanced itinerary quality and computational efficiency over existing methodologies.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a framework combining LLMs for dynamic user preference capture with an enhanced GRASP algorithm for generating feasible, high-quality multi-day travel itineraries. Experiments on Beijing and Tianjin datasets show it outperforms SOTA methods by 4.52%-26.07% in itinerary scores and achieves significant computational efficiency gains.
