AI.motivation: To understand how selective state-space models like Mamba utilize their learned modes, particularly how the selection mechanism dynamically allocates state space across different inputs, and to develop tools for analyzing and potentially compressing these models.
AI.method: Leveraging the diagonal state matrix to decompose each channel's output into per-mode contributions; constructing a per-(layer, channel, window) Gram tensor that yields exact output error for dropping any subset of modes offline; performing frozen-signal counterfactuals to attribute mode migration to B_t vs. timestep; implementing input-scheduled mode pruning based on first-pass usage measurements.
AI.result: The instrument validates against reference implementation with 2.3×10⁻⁷ relative error and predicts pruning error with 5×10⁻⁷ median relative deviation across 4,464 configurations. Trained models show input-dependent mode migration (per-input oracle halves output error of fixed set). Migration attributed primarily to B_t, not timestep. Input-scheduled pruning outperforms static/Hankel/layer-adaptive rankings across all scales (130M–7B) and matches unpruned model at half state budget.
AI.conclusion: The selection mechanism in Mamba models genuinely re-allocates state space based on input content via the write map B_t, and this dynamic allocation can be exploited for efficient pruning—though the paper notes no deployed compute/memory savings are claimed, only demonstration of realizable headroom.

title: MonkeyOCRv2: A Visual-Text Foundation Model for Document AI
summary: Mainstream visual encoders are pretrained on natural images and cannot be effectively applied to document images without document-oriented adaptation, as dense text and fine-grained character strokes demand character-level visual perception. We present MonkeyOCRv2, a visual-text pretrained model for document AI. First, we construct MonkeyDoc v2, to our knowledge the largest document-image pretraining corpus, comprising 113 million images spanning 17 languages. Second, we propose a pretraining strategy that jointly learns image-to-text generation and pixel-level document reconstruction: the former aligns visual representations with textual content, while the latter preserves character strokes and layout details. Extensive experiments are conducted on five representative document analysis tasks, including text recognition, formula recognition, text detection, document tampering detection, and overlapping text segmentation. Replacing the original encoders with MonkeyOCRv2 consistently improves performance across all five tasks. Finally, we validate its effectiveness as the vision encoder of multimodal large language models on the more challenging tasks of document parsing and document understanding. Kept frozen and paired with a lightweight language model, it yields a 0.7B document parsing model that sets a new open-source state-of-the-art on MDPBench, a recent benchmark spanning digital-born and photographed documents across 17 languages, surpassing the previous best 3B dots.mocr by 2.8% absolute with a vision encoder roughly 11$\times$ smaller. The frozen encoder also powers a document understanding model that outperforms counterparts built on CLIP, DINO, and SAM across eight benchmarks under identical training settings. These results suggest that document-oriented visual pretraining can serve as a foundation for document intelligence in its own right.

AI.tldr: MonkeyOCRv2 is a visual-text pretrained model for document AI, trained on the largest document-image corpus (113M images, 17 languages). It jointly learns image-to-text generation and pixel-level document reconstruction, consistently outperforming prior encoders across five document analysis tasks and serving as a strong frozen vision encoder for multimodal LLMs in document parsing and understanding.
AI.motivation: Mainstream visual encoders pretrained on natural images lack character-level visual perception for document images due to dense text and fine-grained character strokes, necessitating document-oriented adaptation.
AI.method: (1) Constructs MonkeyDoc v2, the largest document-image pretraining corpus (113M images, 17 languages). (2) Proposes a pretraining strategy with joint learning of image-to-text generation (aligning visuals with text) and pixel-level document reconstruction (preserving character strokes and layout).
AI.result: Consistent improvement across five document analysis tasks (text recognition, formula recognition, text detection, document tampering detection, overlapping text segmentation). As a frozen encoder with a 0.7B language model, it achieves SOTA on MDPBench (surpassing 3B model by 2.8% absolute, with 11× smaller encoder). Outperforms CLIP/DINO/SAM-based models on eight document understanding benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Document-oriented visual pretraining can serve as a foundational approach for document intelligence, independent of natural-image-based pretraining paradigms.

title: Relaxing Faithfulness with Intervention-Only Causal Discovery
summary: Causal discovery algorithms learn a network that describes the causal dependencies among random variables. A common workflow involves first utilizing conditional independence properties on observational data to determine partially directed causal relationships, then applying interventions to orient the unknown causal directions. A critical assumption for the first step is faithfulness: a requirement that causally linked variables exhibit statistical dependence. Many natural systems include buffering and stabilizing pathways that cancel out to achieve systemic robustness. This cancellation of pathways violates faithfulness, leading causal discovery algorithms to incorrectly remove causal dependencies. In this paper, we argue that hard interventions contain information about the presence/absence of causal linkage that is overlooked in the first stage of structure discovery. We show that a mild assumption -- called intervention-immediacy faithfulness -- that allows cancellations, is sufficient to nonparametrically identify causal structures with hard interventions. These results position interventions as the primary carriers of information about causal structure, which should take precedence over conditional independence testing. To flip the paradigm, we also specify equivalence classes when the identification criteria are not met due to limitations in the scope of interventions.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that hard interventions can identify causal structures even when faithfulness is violated due to pathway cancellations, proposing intervention-immediacy faithfulness as a milder assumption that allows interventions to take precedence over conditional independence testing in causal discovery.
AI.motivation: Traditional causal discovery relies on faithfulness assumption, but many natural systems have buffering/stabilizing pathways that cancel out (violating faithfulness), causing algorithms to miss true causal dependencies. The authors aim to address this limitation.
AI.method: The authors propose using hard interventions as primary carriers of causal information, introducing a milder assumption called "intervention-immediacy faithfulness" that allows for pathway cancellations. They show this is sufficient for nonparametric identification of causal structures.
AI.result: They demonstrate that hard interventions contain overlooked information about causal linkages, and show that intervention-immediacy faithfulness is sufficient to nonparametrically identify causal structures even when faithfulness is violated.
AI.conclusion: The paper proposes flipping the paradigm: interventions should take precedence over conditional independence testing in causal discovery. They also specify equivalence classes for cases where identification criteria are not fully met due to limited intervention scope.

title: Actor as Its Own Critic: Unifying Region Understanding and Localization via CycleGRPO
summary: This paper introduces Actor as Its Own Critic, a unified reinforcement learning framework, Cycle Group Relative Policy Optimization (CycleGRPO), that jointly optimizes region understanding and localization for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Unlike existing separate pipelines, we leverage the inherent duality between the two tasks to construct a self-evaluating reinforcement learning paradigm: "region $\to$ text $\to$ region''. Specifically, a single MLLM first acts as the actor to generate region captions, then immediately transitions to a critic to ground its generated text back in the spatial domain. Therefore, CycleGRPO requires only region inputs, e.g., masks or bounding boxes, entirely bypassing the need for textual ground truths. A quality-aware token-level cycle-consistency reward is employed to assess the semantic discriminability of text captions via their physical localization accuracy. Empirically, built upon SAMTok, our CycleGRPO framework successfully bootstraps both capabilities simultaneously. Without any task-specific fine-tuning, the framework yields consistent performance gains across a wide range of benchmarks, including region captioning, region VQA, grounded dialogue, and referring segmentation. Overall, CycleGRPO offers a straightforward and scalable way to advance pixel-level capabilities in MLLMs. Code and models are released at https://github.com/devinxzhang/CycleGRPO.

AI.tldr: CycleGRPO is a unified reinforcement learning framework that enables a single MLLM to jointly learn region understanding and localization via a self-evaluating "region→text→region" cycle, requiring only region inputs (masks/boxes) without textual ground truths, achieving consistent performance gains across multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing pipelines treat region understanding and localization as separate tasks, ignoring their inherent duality. The goal is to unify them in a single framework that bypasses the need for costly textual ground truth annotations.
AI.method: CycleGRPO uses a single MLLM as both actor (generating region captions) and critic (grounding text back to spatial domain), forming a "region→text→region" cycle. A quality-aware token-level cycle-consistency reward evaluates semantic discriminability via localization accuracy. Built on SAMTok, no task-specific fine-tuning is required.
AI.result: Consistent performance gains across region captioning, region VQA, grounded dialogue, and referring segmentation benchmarks without any task-specific fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: CycleGRPO provides a straightforward, scalable approach to advance pixel-level capabilities in MLLMs by jointly bootstrapping region understanding and localization through self-evaluating reinforcement learning.

title: Transformer-Guided Swarm Intelligence for Frugal Neural Architecture Search
summary: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has automated the design of deep learning models but traditionally requires massive computational resources, often measured in thousands of GPU-days. In this paper, we propose a frugal and memetic NAS framework designed to democratize architecture design on consumer-grade hardware. Our approach combines the global macro-search capabilities of an autoregressive Transformer controller, trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL), with the local micro-exploitation of an Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm. To prevent premature convergence during the RL phase, we introduce a dynamic entropy mechanism that forces topological exploration upon detection of performance stagnation. Evaluated on a standard GPU (NVIDIA RTX 3060), our hybrid method effectively resolves the "cold-start" problem inherent in metaheuristics. By algorithmically penalizing network depth, our framework actively mitigates model bloat: on the CIFAR-10 dataset, it discovers an efficient architecture reaching 84.85% accuracy with only $\sim$174,000 parameters (significantly smaller than standard baselines like ResNet-20) in 3 hours of search time. Furthermore, we demonstrate the framework's flexibility by applying it to credit card fraud detection, directly optimizing the F1-Score on highly imbalanced tabular data to reach a F1-Score of 0.71 with a compact network of $\sim$4,600 parameters. These results suggest that our approach can yield tailored, accessible, and highly parameter-efficient deep learning models suitable for edge deployment.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a frugal and memetic NAS framework combining an autoregressive Transformer controller (trained via RL) with an Artificial Bee Colony algorithm for local exploitation, enabling efficient architecture search on consumer-grade GPUs. It achieves 84.85% accuracy on CIFAR-10 with ~174K parameters in 3 hours on an RTX 3060, and reaches an F1-Score of 0.71 on credit card fraud detection with ~4.6K parameters.
AI.motivation: Traditional NAS requires massive computational resources (thousands of GPU-days), limiting accessibility. The goal is to democratize architecture design on consumer-grade hardware while maintaining search effectiveness.
AI.method: A hybrid memetic NAS framework combining global macro-search via an autoregressive Transformer controller trained with RL for global exploration, and local micro-exploitation via an Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm. A dynamic entropy mechanism prevents premature convergence during RL. Network depth is algorithmically penalized to mitigate model bloat.
AI.result: On CIFAR-10: 84.85% accuracy with ~174K parameters in 3 hours on an RTX 3060. On credit card fraud detection: F1-Score of 0.71 with ~4.6K parameters. Resolves the cold-start problem in metaheuristics and produces significantly smaller models than baselines like ResNet-20.
AI.conclusion: The approach yields tailored, accessible, and highly parameter-efficient deep learning models suitable for edge deployment, effectively democratizing NAS on consumer hardware.

title: GB-SVFBP: Gaussian-Based Shift-Variant FBP neural network
comment: Accepted for poster presentation at the 18th International Meeting on Fully Three-Dimensional Image Reconstruction in Radiology and Nuclear Medicine (Fully3D 2025), Shanghai, China, May 27-30, 2025
summary: This paper proposes a Gaussian-Based Shift-Variant filtered backprojection (FBP) neural network, which is designed for the efficient reconstruction of non-circular trajectory cone beam computed tomography. The traditional differentiable shift-variant FBP model consists of a filtering component and a backprojection process. The filtering component includes operations such as weightings, differentiations, a 2D Radon transform, and a 2D backprojection. The proposed methods build on this framework by introducing a trainable 2D Gaussian model to represent the trajectory-related part in the filtering process, achieving a substantial reduction in the number of trainable parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model reduces the parameter count by 99%, while only sacrificing a slight amount of reconstruction quality. Furthermore, the training time for each trajectory is reduced to one-fourth of the original, significantly accelerating convergence. These enhancements demonstrate a considerable augmentation in the model's practicality and effectiveness, making it a valuable asset for real-world applications.

AI.tldr: Proposes a Gaussian-Based Shift-Variant FBP neural network that reduces trainable parameters by 99% and training time by 75% for non-circular trajectory CBCT reconstruction, with minimal quality loss.
AI.motivation: To improve the efficiency and practicality of differentiable shift-variant FBP models for non-circular trajectory cone beam CT reconstruction by reducing the high parameter count and long training times.
AI.method: Introduces a trainable 2D Gaussian model to represent the trajectory-related part in the filtering process of the shift-variant FBP framework, replacing the original parameter-heavy components.
AI.result: Parameter count reduced by 99%, training time per trajectory reduced to one-fourth of the original, with only slight reconstruction quality degradation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Gaussian-based approach significantly enhances model practicality and effectiveness, making it suitable for real-world non-circular trajectory CBCT applications.

title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
comment: 58 pages, 13 figures, 30 tables; project page: https://xzx34.github.io/unfair-judge/
summary: Existing studies of LLM-as-judge scoring bias work predominantly at the input-output level: they perturb inputs, measure score deltas, and propose prompt-level mitigations. We argue that the same biases admit a representation-level account in the judge's hidden state, complementary to the input-output view and operationally useful in ways it does not afford. We report three findings, across seven judges, seven bias types, and nine benchmarks. Geometry: baseline judging inputs occupy a tight activation manifold while biased inputs are displaced along a low-dimensional, type-specific subspace that sharpens with depth and is recovered consistently by three families of estimators. Causal control: steering hidden states along this subspace drives scoring in both directions, forward shifts reproducing biased scoring on clean inputs and reverse shifts restoring baseline scoring on biased ones, while matched-norm random directions produce shifts an order of magnitude smaller. Operational: a simple linear projection onto the same bias-direction features anticipates judge failures on three entirely unseen benchmarks, substantially outperforming text-based alternatives. Reading bias as activation geometry, rather than as input-output noise, unifies geometric structure, causal control, and operational prediction within a single framework. The project page is available at https://xzx34.github.io/unfair-judge/

AI.tldr: LLM-as-judge scoring biases can be understood through hidden state geometry, enabling causal control and operational prediction beyond input-output analysis.
AI.motivation: Existing studies analyze LLM-as-judge bias only at the input-output level, missing the complementary representational perspective that could enable more fundamental understanding and mitigation.
AI.method: Analyze hidden state geometry of judges (7 models, 7 bias types, 9 benchmarks), identify low-dimensional bias subspaces via three estimator families, perform causal steering along bias directions, and use linear projection for failure prediction.
AI.result: Biased inputs form type-specific low-dimensional subspaces; steering along these subspaces drives scoring bidirectionally; linear projection on bias features predicts judge failures on unseen benchmarks, outperforming text-based methods.
AI.conclusion: Reading bias as activation geometry unifies geometric characterization, causal control, and operational prediction into a single framework, offering advantages over input-output approaches.

title: FoundationGeo: Learning Spatial Pixel-Wise Fields for Monocular Metric Geometry
comment: 28 pages, 8 figures. Accepted to ECCV 2026. Muxin Liu and Xiaoyang Lyu contributed equally. Shaoshuai Shi and Xiaojuan Qi are corresponding authors. Project page: https://mx-liu6.github.io/FoundationGeo-web/
summary: We present FoundationGeo, a two-stage framework that explicitly bridges relative and metric prediction via spatial calibration and principled data design. Stage 1 learns a high-fidelity, affine-invariant geometry model by initializing with DINOv3 and training on a curated 10.2M-sample multi-domain corpus with complementary local-detail supervision, yielding sharp boundaries and strong cross-domain generalization. Stage 2 moves beyond global scaling by introducing lightweight pixel-wise calibration fields for metric estimation: a scale field for spatially varying metric alignment and a ray-direction correction field that mitigates directional bias in point-map geometry, together producing metrically consistent 3D point maps. Beyond model design, we identify camera intrinsic coverage, especially focal length distribution mismatch between training and test data, as a key bottleneck for zero-shot metric generalization: performance drops sharply when test intrinsics fall outside the training distribution. To address this, we synthesize additional training data across diverse focal lengths using a Blender-based data engine, repairing under-covered focal regimes and improving robustness under intrinsic shift. Extensive zero-shot evaluations across seven benchmarks show that FoundationGeo significantly strengthens cross-domain robustness, staying near the top across diverse domains while avoiding the sharp cross-domain performance drops observed in other methods. This consistency translates into the best overall performance, surpassing heavier baselines by over 5.2% on average.

AI.tldr: FoundationGeo is a two-stage framework for metric 3D geometry estimation that bridges relative and metric prediction via pixel-wise calibration fields and a Blender-based data engine addressing focal length distribution mismatch, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot generalization across seven benchmarks with over 5.2% improvement over heavier baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing methods struggle with cross-domain generalization in metric 3D estimation, particularly due to (1) the gap between affine-invariant relative depth and metric prediction, and (2) camera intrinsic distribution mismatch (especially focal length) between training and test data, causing sharp performance drops in zero-shot settings.
AI.method: A two-stage framework: Stage 1 trains an affine-invariant geometry model (initialized with DINOv3) on a 10.2M-sample multi-domain corpus with local-detail supervision. Stage 2 introduces lightweight pixel-wise calibration fields—a scale field for spatially varying metric alignment and a ray-direction correction field for directional bias mitigation. Additionally, a Blender-based data engine synthesizes training data across diverse focal lengths to repair under-covered intrinsic regimes.
AI.result: Extensive zero-shot evaluations across seven benchmarks show FoundationGeo achieves strong cross-domain robustness, stays near the top across diverse domains without sharp performance drops, and surpasses heavier baselines by over 5.2% on average.
AI.conclusion: Bridging relative and metric geometry via spatial calibration and addressing intrinsic distribution mismatch via data synthesis are effective strategies for robust zero-shot metric 3D estimation.

title: Invariant Learning Dynamics of Transformers in Inductive Reasoning Tasks
summary: We present a theoretical framework to explain the emergence of inductive reasoning abilities in Transformer language models. While previous works on Transformer learning dynamics have so far been mostly tied to specific tasks, we study a generalized class of inductive tasks that unifies several synthetic tasks known in the literature, including in-context n-grams and multi-hop reasoning. In this class, we theoretically prove that the training dynamics of attention models can be confined to a highly interpretable, low-dimensional invariant manifold. On this manifold, the learning dynamics are captured by a handful of interpretable coordinates rather than millions of parameters, making both theoretical and empirical analysis more tractable. Using this framework, we characterize how data statistics govern the competition between in-context and in-weights learning, we study how random initializations determine the `winning' circuit when multiple solutions are possible, and we demonstrate that the coordinate frame associated with the manifold can be used to automatically detect which circuits have been learned in trained models. By casting circuit formation as a low-dimensional dynamical phenomenon, we take a step toward a predictive theory of how Transformers learn.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework showing that Transformer language models' training dynamics for inductive reasoning tasks can be reduced to a low-dimensional invariant manifold, where learning is governed by a few interpretable coordinates rather than millions of parameters. It explains the competition between in-context and in-weights learning, how random initializations determine which circuit emerges, and how circuit detection can be automated.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified theoretical explanation for the emergence of inductive reasoning abilities in Transformers, moving beyond task-specific analyses to a generalized framework that makes learning dynamics more tractable and interpretable.
AI.method: The authors define a generalized class of inductive tasks unifying synthetic benchmarks like in-context n-grams and multi-hop reasoning. They prove theoretically that attention model training dynamics are confined to a low-dimensional invariant manifold, and analyze how data statistics, random initializations, and circuit formation behave within this reduced coordinate space.
AI.result: The training dynamics can be captured by a handful of interpretable coordinates. They characterize how data statistics govern in-context vs. in-weights learning competition, how random initialization selects the winning circuit among multiple solutions, and how the manifold's coordinate frame enables automatic circuit detection.
AI.conclusion: By reframing circuit formation as a low-dimensional dynamical phenomenon, this work takes a step toward a predictive theory of how Transformers learn inductive reasoning capabilities.

title: Similarity-Guided Curriculum Fine-Tuning of LLMs for Neural Architecture Synthesis
summary: Introduce a MinHash-based similarity scheduling framework that constructs a progressive curriculum over neural architecture code for LLM-based neural architecture search (NAS). Using 128-permutation MinHash signatures over normalised 7-gram source code shingles, we partition the reference pool into similarity bands and present them in increasing architectural heterogeneity, with the best LoRA adapter from each stage merged cumulatively into the backbone. We evaluate the framework on OlympicCoder-7B within the LEMUR benchmark on CIFAR-10 image classification, generating N =15 candidate architectures per epoch across six progressive fine-tuning steps. The curriculum achieves 60% peak success rate at the high-similarity level without post-processing repair. A 2*2 ablation at the most diverse level curriculum versus base model, with versus without partial interface repair reveals that without repair the base model (47% peak SR) substantially outperforms the curriculum model (7% SR), while adding partial repair brings both to 53% SR. This pattern is consistent with merge-level weight drift progressively erasing evaluator-interface priors, and suggests that interface repair and curriculum scheduling target distinct failure modes. We further report a cross-dataset transfer observation on SVHN, where direct base-model generation without curriculum warmup yields 27% peak SR at substantially lower accuracy (60.5%) than the CIFAR-10 equivalent, consistent with the increased synthesis difficulty of the unq-family anchor architecture.

AI.tldr: A MinHash-based progressive curriculum scheduling framework for LLM-based NAS, evaluated on CIFAR-10 and SVHN, showing curriculum design and interface repair address distinct failure modes.
AI.motivation: To improve LLM-based neural architecture search by structuring the reference code space with a progressive similarity curriculum, mitigating weight drift and interface corruption during LoRA merging.
AI.method: Uses 128-permutation MinHash signatures over normalized 7-gram source code shingles to partition NAS reference pools into similarity bands. Presents architectures in increasing heterogeneity, cumulatively merging LoRA adapters. Evaluated on OlympicCoder-7B with LEMUR benchmark, generating 15 candidates per epoch over 6 fine-tuning steps.
AI.result: Curriculum achieves 60% peak success rate at high-similarity level without post-processing repair. Ablation shows base model (47% SR) outperforms curriculum (7% SR) without repair; both reach 53% SR with partial repair. Cross-dataset transfer on SVHN yields 27% SR at 60.5% accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Interface repair and curriculum scheduling address distinct failure modes: curriculum manages architectural heterogeneity, while repair counters merge-level weight drift that erases evaluator-interface priors.

title: Requential Coding: Pushing the Limits of Model Compression with Self-Generated Training Data
summary: Compression is fundamental to intelligence. A model that can represent its training data as a short code has discovered regularities that enable generalization. Large neural networks may learn functions far simpler than their parameter counts suggest, but it is challenging to construct codes that realize this simplicity. Parameter-based methods such as quantization produce code lengths that scale with model size, insensitive to how much information the parameters store. Prequential coding bypasses this issue by compressing the training trajectory, but codes the exact data sequence regardless of how much the model learns, yielding large codes when the data has high entropy. We introduce requential coding, where a teacher model selects training samples drawn from the student's own distribution. The student's code records only these selections, which cost bits only where teacher and student disagree. The resulting code length is independent of parameter count and data entropy, and often orders of magnitude shorter than the prequential counterpart, with an advantage that grows with scale. This compression sheds light on phenomena inaccessible to prior compressors. Holding loss fixed, larger models and ensembles compress to much smaller sizes despite more parameters. Plugged into a PAC-Bayes bound, the requential code yields state-of-the-art generalization guarantees for billion-parameter LLMs, outperforming bounds built on aggressive post-training quantization even granted zero error. The bound tightens with scale in the compute-optimal regime, as models become increasingly compressible relative to dataset size. The same code predicts that models gradually overfit when trained for multiple epochs. It also isolates the learnable information in a dataset from its unpredictable, random content, revealing that lower-entropy text holds far more learnable structure than higher-entropy image data.

AI.tldr: Requential coding compresses models by having a teacher select training samples where the student model disagrees, producing code lengths independent of parameter count and data entropy, often orders of magnitude shorter than prequential codes, with advantages that grow with scale.
AI.motivation: Existing compression methods for neural networks fail to capture true model simplicity: parameter-based methods (e.g., quantization) scale with model size regardless of information content, while prequential coding compresses the exact data sequence regardless of how much the model learns, yielding large codes for high-entropy data.
AI.method: Introduces requential coding where a teacher model selects training samples drawn from the student's own distribution; the student's code records only these selections, costing bits only where teacher and student disagree, making code length independent of parameter count and data entropy.
AI.result: Requential codes are often orders of magnitude shorter than prequential codes with advantages that grow with scale; larger models and ensembles compress more despite more parameters; plugged into PAC-Bayes bounds, yields state-of-the-art generalization guarantees for billion-parameter LLMs, outperforming quantization-based bounds; bounds tighten with scale in the compute-optimal regime; predicts gradual overfitting in multi-epoch training; isolates learnable information from random content, showing lower-entropy text has more learnable structure than higher-entropy image data.
AI.conclusion: Requential coding provides a fundamentally better compression framework for understanding neural network generalization, scaling properties, and the nature of learnable information in data.

title: Backbone-Agnostic Perturbation-Induced Uncertainty Learning for End-to-End Real-World Image Dehazing
summary: Real-world paired image dehazing remains challenging because haze degradation is spatially non-uniform, illumination-dependent, and physically ambiguous even when haze-free references are available. Existing end-to-end restoration networks usually formulate dehazing as a deterministic mapping from a hazy observation to a clean target, leaving the uncertainty hidden in degraded features, haze priors, and cross-domain negative samples insufficiently explored. In this paper, we propose Backbone-Agnostic Perturbation-Induced Uncertainty Learning (BPUL), a plug-and-play uncertainty learning framework for end-to-end real-world image dehazing. BPUL first introduces a Learnable Perturbation-induced Uncertainty Modulator (LPUM) that estimates channel-wise and spatial-wise feature sensitivity through reparameterized stochastic perturbations. It then develops a Prior-informed Uncertainty-guided Reconstruction Module (PURM), which exploits transmission and atmospheric-light priors to reconstruct the hazy observation from the restored result and enforce degradation consistency. Furthermore, we propose a Dual-space Domain-diversified Distribution-aware Contrastive Loss ($D^3$CL) to regularize both clean restoration and hazy reconstruction spaces with real-world and synthetic negatives. Experiments on five real-world paired benchmarks show that BPUL consistently improves multiple representative backbones. Since only LPUM is retained during inference while PURM and $D^3$CL are used as training-time constraints, BPUL brings substantial restoration gains with only marginal additional inference overhead.

AI.tldr: BPUL is a plug-and-play uncertainty learning framework for real-world image dehazing that improves multiple backbones by modeling feature uncertainty, enforcing haze degradation consistency, and using contrastive learning with real/synthetic negatives, while adding minimal inference cost.
AI.motivation: Existing end-to-end dehazing networks treat the task as a deterministic mapping, failing to address the spatial non-uniformity, illumination dependency, and physical ambiguity of real-world haze, leaving uncertainty in degraded features, haze priors, and cross-domain negative samples underexplored.
AI.method: BPUL consists of three components: (1) Learnable Perturbation-induced Uncertainty Modulator (LPUM) for channel-wise and spatial-wise feature sensitivity estimation via reparameterized stochastic perturbations; (2) Prior-informed Uncertainty-guided Reconstruction Module (PURM) that uses transmission and atmospheric-light priors to reconstruct hazy input from restored output for degradation consistency; (3) Dual-space Domain-diversified Distribution-aware Contrastive Loss (D^3CL) that regularizes both clean and haze reconstruction spaces using real-world and synthetic negatives.
AI.result: Experiments on five real-world paired benchmarks show consistent improvements across multiple representative backbone architectures. Only LPUM is retained at inference; PURM and D^3CL serve as training-time constraints, yielding substantial restoration gains with marginal additional inference overhead.
AI.conclusion: Modeling uncertainty explicitly via perturbations, enforcing haze-consistency reconstruction, and leveraging contrastive learning with diverse negatives effectively bridges the gap between synthetic and real-world dehazing, offering a lightweight plug-and-play solution.

title: Motion4Motion: Motion Transfer Across Subjects at Inference
summary: This work explores the motion transfer from one video to another, which is crucial in animation for diverse characters. Previously, video motion transfer has been largely explored between human and human-like characters, enabling a lot of applications in digital creation. However, these approaches encounter a main limitation. Specifically, related technical pipelines heavily rely on a predefined human skeleton structure and accordingly require skeleton-conditional model training. On the one hand, these methods are difficult to generalize to diverse characters, such as animals from different species, while preserving their unique motion styles. On the other hand, labeled data in diverse skeletons is limited, which additionally restricts the large-scale training for the task. In this paper, we jump out of the skeleton-based motion transfer framework and propose a training-free motion transfer framework, named Motion4Motion. Motion4Motionmodels the motion flow of the character in a video instead of skeletons, which makes motion transfer across species easier. Extensive experimental results and novel applications show our methods outperform baselines impressively. Project page is available at https://lhchen.top/Motion4Motion.

AI.tldr: Motion4Motion is a training-free, skeleton-free framework for cross-species motion transfer between videos, using motion flow modeling instead of predefined skeleton structures to enable motion transfer across diverse characters (e.g., different animal species) while preserving their unique motion styles.
AI.motivation: Existing skeleton-based motion transfer methods are limited to human/human-like characters because they rely on predefined skeleton structures and require skeleton-conditional training, making them difficult to generalize to diverse characters (e.g., animals from different species) while preserving unique motion styles, and labeled skeleton data is scarce for large-scale training.
AI.method: Motion4Motion proposes a training-free motion transfer framework that models motion flow of characters in a video instead of using skeletons, bypassing the need for skeleton-conditional model training and enabling cross-species motion transfer.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show Motion4Motion outperforms baselines impressively, with novel applications demonstrated in cross-species motion transfer.
AI.conclusion: Jumping out of the skeleton-based paradigm and adopting motion flow modeling is an effective training-free approach for generalizable cross-species motion transfer in animation.

title: Event-RGB Adaptive Tracking for Nighttime Highway Perception
summary: Intelligent Transportation Systems deployed on highways predominantly rely on conventional RGB cameras for traffic perception and vehicle tracking. However, highway environments present unique challenges: the absence of artificial lighting infrastructure, combined with high vehicle velocities, results in severely degraded perception performance under low-light conditions. Specifically, nighttime scenarios suffer from motion blur, insufficient exposure, and poor signal-to-noise ratios, which catastrophically impair the reliability of RGB-based sensing systems. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Joint Event-RGB Adaptive Tracking (JEAT) framework. Unlike existing multi-sensor trackers constrained by rigid, hard-coded prioritization, JEAT merges asynchronous event streams and RGB frames into a unified joint data association optimization. By employing an Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter to continuously estimate measurement noise via NIS statistics, the framework dynamically weights and fuses both modalities, optimally harnessing event streams during dark or high-speed motion while leveraging RGB frames under bright or static conditions. Furthermore, given the absence of publicly available datasets tailored for event-based highway perception with diverse environmental conditions, we present SEHN, a large-scale synthetic dataset generated using the CARLA simulator. Our dataset encompasses diverse environmental conditions (daytime, nighttime, nighttime with out artificial lighting) and varying traffic densities, providing synchronized RGB imagery and event streams to facilitate multi-modal fusion research. Our code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/haidongwang96/SEHN.

AI.tldr: Proposes JEAT, a joint event-RGB adaptive tracking framework for highway perception under low-light conditions, and introduces SEHN, a large-scale synthetic dataset for event-based highway perception.
AI.motivation: Highway environments lack artificial lighting and involve high vehicle velocities, causing RGB cameras to fail under low-light conditions due to motion blur, insufficient exposure, and poor signal-to-noise ratios.
AI.method: JEAT merges asynchronous event streams and RGB frames via unified joint data association optimization. An Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter continuously estimates measurement noise using NIS statistics to dynamically weight and fuse modalities. SEHN dataset generated with CARLA simulator under diverse conditions.
AI.result: No empirical results reported in the abstract; the paper introduces the framework and dataset. SEHN provides synchronized RGB and event data across daytime, nighttime, and nighttime without artificial lighting scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed JEAT framework and SEHN dataset aim to address RGB camera failures in low-light highway tracking by adaptively fusing event and RGB modalities.

title: Feature-Space Guided Diffusion for Realistic Ultrasound Image Synthesis
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Pre-review manuscript version of a paper accepted at DGM4MICCAI 2026
summary: Conditional diffusion models can generate anatomically plausible medical ultrasound (US) images, but anatomical plausibility alone does not ensure realistic B-mode appearance. Most US pipelines adapt standard generative architectures and condition them on anatomical masks, or use guidance mechanisms that reinforce the same anatomical signal. However, B-mode US images are shaped by acquisition-dependent properties such as speckle texture, tissue contrast, and attenuation. Using a frozen US foundation model, we show that standard conditional diffusion baselines remain separated from real images in representation space. In this work, we propose Feature-Space Candidate Guidance (FSCG), a training-free sampling strategy to reduce this gap. At sampling time, FSCG applies local k-NN feature correction and selects the best of multiple stochastic candidates according to their feature-space energy. In this way, the mask defines the anatomy, while FSCG steers samples toward the real US domain. Across three different datasets, FSCG reduces average FID64 by 56\%, FID192 by 57\%, and nearest-neighbour feature distance by 47\% over standard conditional diffusion sampling, outperforming alternative inference-time guidance baselines. The results suggest that domain-aware feature representations can reveal and reduce realism gaps in medical diffusion synthesis without retraining the generator. Our code is available at https://github.com/marinadominguez/FSCG.

AI.tldr: FSCG is a training-free sampling strategy that uses feature-space guidance with a frozen US foundation model to reduce the realism gap between conditional diffusion-generated and real B-mode ultrasound images, achieving significant FID and feature distance improvements across three datasets.
AI.motivation: Standard conditional diffusion models for medical ultrasound generate anatomically plausible images but fail to capture realistic B-mode appearance (speckle texture, tissue contrast, attenuation). There is a domain gap between generated and real US images in representation space that existing methods do not address.
AI.method: Feature-Space Candidate Guidance (FSCG) is a training-free inference-time strategy using a frozen US foundation model. It applies local k-NN feature correction during sampling and selects the best of multiple stochastic candidates based on feature-space energy, steering samples toward the real US domain while the mask defines anatomy.
AI.result: Across three datasets, FSCG reduces average FID64 by 56%, FID192 by 57%, and nearest-neighbour feature distance by 47% over standard conditional diffusion sampling, outperforming alternative inference-time guidance baselines.
AI.conclusion: Domain-aware feature representations from US foundation models can reveal and reduce realism gaps in medical diffusion synthesis without retraining the generator.

title: ABot-3DWorld 0: A Universal World Model to Explore Any 3D Space
summary: We present ABot-3DWorld 0, a universal multimodal 3D world model that turns text, image, and video inputs into high-fidelity, explorable 3D worlds. At the heart of our framework is a unified Spatial Generative Primitive (SGP), a compact tuple of a high-quality panorama and a spatial point cloud that delivers an efficient description of any 3D space. Multimodal inputs are first lifted into this primitive; a 3D-consistent panoramic video generator then explores the primitive along a planned trajectory; finally, our panoramic video reconstruction engine converts the generated video into a clean, photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) world. This pipeline covers two regimes: rich inputs (multi-view sets, casual video) are lifted into the SGP through a geometry-rigorous recovery that mirrors the observed scene, while a single image or sentence is completed generatively into a creative world. The result is one low-barrier engine for general 3D content creation that further anchors generated worlds to geographic points of interest, enabling map-native spatial exploration at consumer scale. Experiments show that ABot-3DWorld 0 sets the state of the art among open-source methods and demonstrates stronger scene fidelity than Marble under rich multimodal inputs.

AI.tldr: ABot-3DWorld 0 is a universal multimodal 3D world model that converts text, image, and video inputs into high-fidelity, explorable 3D worlds using a unified Spatial Generative Primitive (SGP) consisting of a panorama and point cloud, achieving state-of-the-art scene fidelity among open-source methods.
AI.motivation: To create a low-barrier, universal engine for general 3D content creation that accepts diverse multimodal inputs (text, image, video) and produces high-fidelity, explorable 3D worlds, while also enabling map-native spatial exploration at consumer scale.
AI.method: A three-stage pipeline: (1) multimodal inputs are lifted into a unified Spatial Generative Primitive (SGP) — a compact tuple of a high-quality panorama and spatial point cloud; (2) a 3D-consistent panoramic video generator explores the primitive along a planned trajectory; (3) a panoramic video reconstruction engine converts the generated video into a clean, photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) world. Supports two regimes: geometry-rigorous recovery for rich inputs (multi-view, video) and generative completion for sparse inputs (single image, sentence).
AI.result: Sets state-of-the-art among open-source methods and demonstrates stronger scene fidelity than Marble under rich multimodal inputs.
AI.conclusion: ABot-3DWorld 0 provides a universal, low-barrier engine for general 3D content creation that anchors generated worlds to geographic points of interest, enabling map-native spatial exploration at consumer scale.

title: Illuminant-Adaptive 3D Lookup Tables for Camera Color Correction
summary: Color correction is a key component of camera image signal processing (ISP) pipelines, encompassing illuminant discounting and colorimetric mapping of device-dependent sensor responses to device-independent color spaces, such as CIE XYZ. Despite extensive research, accurate color correction remains challenging due to the non-linear relationship between camera sensor responses and CIE XYZ color space, as well as to the increasing presence of highly chromatic and spectrally complex LED illuminants. We propose a color correction framework based on illuminant-adaptive three-dimensional lookup tables (LUTs), which we call Color Correction LUT (C$^2$LUT). Our method combines a chromaticity-aware illuminant representation with a non-linear color transformation, enabling accurate correction under illuminants spanning a wide range of chromaticities and spectral complexities. We employ Tucker tensor decomposition to represent the LUTs, ensuring that computational requirements remain sufficiently low for deployment in camera ISPs. In addition, we introduce a large-scale illuminants dataset comprising 1,473 spectral power distributions, with different chromaticities and spectral profiles. Experiments across multiple cameras, illuminants, reflectance datasets, and real captured images demonstrate consistent improvements over existing methods for color correction, reducing CIE $ΔE_{00}$ by up to 20% and angular error by up to 18% while remaining compatible with modern camera hardware constraints. Code and datasets are available at https://github.com/claudiom4sir/C2LUT.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes C²LUT, an illuminant-adaptive 3D lookup table framework for camera color correction that uses Tucker tensor decomposition for efficiency and a new large-scale illuminant dataset, achieving up to 20% reduction in CIE ΔE₀₀ and 18% angular error reduction across multiple cameras.
AI.motivation: Accurate color correction remains challenging due to the non-linear relationship between camera sensor responses and CIE XYZ color space, as well as the increasing prevalence of highly chromatic and spectrally complex LED illuminants.
AI.method: The method combines a chromaticity-aware illuminant representation with non-linear color transformation using illuminant-adaptive 3D lookup tables (C²LUT), with Tucker tensor decomposition to reduce computational requirements for deployment in camera ISPs. A large-scale illuminant dataset of 1,473 spectral power distributions is also introduced.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple cameras, illuminants, reflectance datasets, and real captured images demonstrate consistent improvements over existing methods, reducing CIE ΔE₀₀ by up to 20% and angular error by up to 18% while remaining compatible with modern camera hardware constraints.
AI.conclusion: C²LUT provides accurate illuminant-adaptive color correction suitable for deployment in camera ISPs, supported by a new large-scale illuminant dataset and demonstrated performance gains over existing approaches.

title: SVI360: Spherical Video Interpolation
comment: Accepted at ECCV 2026. Code and trained models are available at: https://icb-vision-ai.github.io/video360_interpolation/
summary: This paper addresses the problem of omnidirectional video interpolation, which plays an essential role in applications such as virtual reality and immersive video enhancement. Existing video interpolation methods are not well-suited for spherical videos, as they have difficulty handling severe distortions close to the poles. To address this issue, we propose SVI360, a dual-branch framework that combines the image frame and its rotated orthogonal view to deal with these distortions. The core methodological aspect of the approach is to reinforce equivariance of the flow displacements between the original and orthogonal views to improve intermediate frame prediction. Experiments show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in interpolation quality while maintaining accurate optical flow in four different public benchmarks. Code and pre-trained models are available at: https://icb-vision-ai.github.io/video360_interpolation/

AI.tldr: SVI360 is a dual-branch framework for omnidirectional video interpolation that uses rotated orthogonal views to handle spherical distortions near the poles, achieving state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing video interpolation methods struggle with spherical videos due to severe distortions near the poles. This paper aims to address this limitation to improve applications like virtual reality and immersive video enhancement.
AI.method: The proposed SVI360 is a dual-branch framework that combines the original image frame with its rotated orthogonal view. The key innovation is reinforcing equivariance of flow displacements between these two views to improve intermediate frame prediction.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in interpolation quality and maintains accurate optical flow across four public benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The dual-branch approach with equivariance constraints effectively addresses polar distortions in spherical video interpolation, and the method generalizes well across multiple benchmarks.

title: GFR-SAM: Training-Free Referring Camouflaged Object Segmentation via Cross-Image Prompting
summary: Referring Camouflaged Object Detection (Ref-COD) requires segmenting hidden targets guided by reference cues. While supervised methods are annotation-heavy and training-free approaches via sparse point-prompting are sensitive to localization errors, we propose GFR-SAM, a robust three-stage training-free framework. GFR-SAM shifts the paradigm from fragile point-matching to a "Generate-Filter-Refine" pipeline. First, we introduce In-Context Exemplar-guided Segmentation, empowering SAM3 with cross-image inference to generate candidate masks via holistic visual exemplars, bypassing its native intra-image constraints. Second, a Region-Global Contrastive Filtering module ranks candidates through DINOv3-based prototypical alignment, effectively suppressing background distractors. Finally, a Geometric-Semantic Refinement module synergizes bounding box and text prompts to recover fine-grained boundaries and enhance instance recall. Evaluated on the R2C7K benchmark, GFR-SAM outperforms existing training-free methods by 8.7\% in weighted F-measure ($F_β^w$) and competes with supervised state-of-the-art counterparts. Ultimately, this work underscores the potential of unlocking SAM3's latent capability for cross-image In-Context prompting, establishing a robust, training-free paradigm that effectively bridges the gap between general-purpose foundation models and specialized, label-intensive perception tasks without the need for task-specific fine-tuning.

AI.tldr: GFR-SAM proposes a training-free, three-stage "Generate-Filter-Refine" framework for Referring Camouflaged Object Detection (Ref-COD) that overcomes the limitations of supervised methods (annotation-heavy) and sparse point-prompting (sensitive to localization errors). It achieves 8.7% improvement in weighted F-measure over existing training-free methods on the R2C7K benchmark and competes with supervised approaches.
AI.motivation: Existing Ref-COD methods suffer from either heavy annotation requirements (supervised) or sensitivity to localization errors (training-free point-prompting). There is a need for a robust training-free paradigm that bridges foundation models and specialized perception tasks without fine-tuning.
AI.method: Three-stage training-free framework: (1) In-Context Exemplar-guided Segmentation uses SAM3 with cross-image inference to generate candidate masks via holistic visual exemplars; (2) Region-Global Contrastive Filtering ranks candidates through DINOv3-based prototypical alignment to suppress background distractors; (3) Geometric-Semantic Refinement synergizes bounding box and text prompts to recover fine-grained boundaries and enhance instance recall.
AI.result: Outperforms existing training-free methods by 8.7% in weighted F-measure ($F_β^w$) on the R2C7K benchmark and achieves competitive performance against supervised state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: This work unlocks SAM3's latent cross-image In-Context prompting capability, establishing a robust training-free paradigm that effectively bridges the gap between general-purpose foundation models and specialized, label-intensive perception tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Higher-Order Cell Tracking Transformer
summary: Reconstructing lineages from live-imaging microscopy requires linking cell detections across time, including through cell divisions. A common approach is to construct a candidate graph and associate cell segmentations (nodes) across frames. However, these and other existing methods overlook two structural obstacles in candidate tracking graphs: (i) cell divisions entangle distinct lineage paths in the node embedding space, and (ii) edges sharing a node have near-random label agreement, so the candidate-graph topology carries no useful information for graph neural networks to aggregate. We propose the \textbf{Higher-Order Cell Tracking Transformer} (HOCT), an edge-centric architecture in which candidate cell links attend to one another under a 3D geometric prior, resolving both issues. Evaluated on the Cell Tracking Challenge and a bacteria division benchmark, HOCT achieves state-of-the-art results without deep pre-trained image encoders. Moreover, the proposed approach is easier to fine-tune, quickly reducing tracking errors by 59% with 400 annotations in a human-in-the-loop setting, outperforming LoRA fine-tuning of competing transformer baselines (6.75% improvement).

AI.tldr: HOCT is an edge-centric transformer architecture that resolves structural issues in candidate tracking graphs (entangled lineage paths and uninformative topology) by using a 3D geometric prior for edge attention, achieving SOTA on cell tracking challenges without deep pre-trained encoders and enabling efficient human-in-the-loop fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Existing cell tracking methods overlook two structural obstacles: (1) cell divisions entangle distinct lineage paths in node embedding space, and (2) edges sharing a node have near-random label agreement, making candidate-graph topology uninformative for GNNs.
AI.method: Proposes Higher-Order Cell Tracking Transformer (HOCT), an edge-centric architecture where candidate cell links attend to one another under a 3D geometric prior, avoiding the node-level entanglement and topological uninformative issues.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art results on Cell Tracking Challenge and bacteria division benchmark without deep pre-trained image encoders. In human-in-the-loop setting, reduces tracking errors by 59% with 400 annotations (6.75% improvement over LoRA fine-tuning of competing baselines).
AI.conclusion: HOCT effectively addresses structural graph obstacles in cell tracking with an edge-centric design and geometric prior, offering superior performance and efficient fine-tuning capability.

title: StoryTeller: Training-Free Narrative Grounding for Long-Form Audio Description
comment: Accepted to the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026
summary: Long-form audio description (AD) requires more than describing visible actions: it must preserve characters, events, relationships, and story context across scenes so that blind and low-vision (BLV) audiences can follow a film. Modern video-language models (VLMs) are effective on short clips, but they often treat each moment independently, producing descriptions that miss who characters are, why events matter, and how the current scene connects to earlier narrative context. We propose StoryTeller, a training-free framework for story-aware long-form AD. Instead of relying only on local visual cues, StoryTeller maintains a verified narrative memory that carries forward story-relevant information across scenes, enabling later descriptions to remain coherent, grounded, and contextually informative. Given only raw video and a movie title, StoryTeller can optionally retrieve public movie metadata to resolve names and story context, while accepting only facts that are supported by the video through semantic filtering and VLM verification. The method requires no subtitles, scripts, AD transcripts, aligned captions, character banks, precomputed face identities, or task-specific fine-tuning. To evaluate whether generated AD preserves narrative information, we introduce StoryAD-QA, a question-answering benchmark that tests whether a language model can answer story-context questions using only the generated descriptions. Experiments on standard AD benchmarks and diverse long-form videos show that StoryTeller consistently improves narrative coherence, factual grounding, and story comprehension over strong baselines in automatic, QA-based, and human evaluations.

AI.tldr: StoryTeller is a training-free framework that improves long-form audio description by maintaining verified narrative memory across scenes, ensuring story coherence without requiring scripts, subtitles, or fine-tuning. It is evaluated using StoryAD-QA, a new QA benchmark for narrative comprehension.
AI.motivation: Long-form audio description for BLV audiences requires preserving narrative context (characters, events, relationships) across scenes, but existing VLMs treat each moment independently, producing incoherent descriptions that lack story awareness.
AI.method: StoryTeller uses a verified narrative memory that carries story-relevant information across scenes, optionally retrieves public movie metadata, and applies semantic filtering plus VLM verification to accept only video-supported facts. No subtitles, scripts, or fine-tuning required.
AI.result: StoryTeller consistently improves narrative coherence, factual grounding, and story comprehension over strong baselines in automatic, QA-based, and human evaluations on standard AD benchmarks and diverse long-form videos.
AI.conclusion: Training-free narrative memory integration effectively enables story-aware long-form audio description, and the StoryAD-QA benchmark provides a valid measure of narrative information preservation in generated descriptions.

title: MM-ToolSandBox: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Visual Tool-Calling Agents
summary: We introduce MM-ToolSandBox, a benchmark and evaluation framework for visually grounded tool-calling agents. The framework provides a stateful execution environment spanning 500+ tools across 16 application domains, supporting multi-image, multi-turn tasks where agents must ground progressively arriving visual inputs into executable tool calls while handling realistic conversational phenomena (goal revisions, error corrections, state mutations). An automated scenario generation pipeline produces diverse, visually grounded scenarios through information-flow-guided planning and multi-stage quality filtering, yielding 258 human-verified nominal scenarios and 50 variants targeting interactive UI applications. Evaluating 12 state-of-the-art models, from 4B open-weight to frontier proprietary systems, shows that current models still lack robust visual tool-calling capability: even the best model achieves below 50% success rate. Our failure analysis further reveals that visual precision, not only planning, is a primary bottleneck for capable models: 53% of failures stem from incorrect information extraction from images despite otherwise correct task workflows. A planning-to-precision crossover emerges with scale: smaller models fail at deciding what to do, while larger models fail at perceiving what they see, suggesting fundamentally different research directions for improving models at different capability levels. The framework and the benchmark are publicly available at https://github.com/apple/ml-mmtoolsandbox

AI.tldr: MM-ToolSandBox is a benchmark and evaluation framework for visually grounded tool-calling agents, featuring 500+ tools across 16 domains, multi-image multi-turn tasks, and automated scenario generation. Evaluating 12 models reveals that even the best achieves below 50% success rate, with larger models failing primarily due to visual precision issues rather than planning errors.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks lack stateful execution environments, multi-turn visual grounding, and realistic conversational phenomena for tool-calling agents. There is a need to systematically evaluate how well models can ground progressively arriving visual inputs into executable tool calls while handling goal revisions, error corrections, and state mutations.
AI.method: The framework provides a stateful execution environment with 500+ tools across 16 domains. An automated scenario generation pipeline uses information-flow-guided planning and multi-stage quality filtering, producing 258 human-verified nominal scenarios and 50 UI variants. The authors evaluated 12 models ranging from 4B open-weight to proprietary frontier systems.
AI.result: The best model achieves below 50% success rate. Failure analysis reveals 53% of failures stem from incorrect information extraction from images despite otherwise correct task workflows. A planning-to-precision crossover emerges: smaller models fail at deciding what to do (planning), while larger models fail at perceiving what they see (visual precision).
AI.conclusion: Current models lack robust visual tool-calling capability. Visual precision, not just planning, is a primary bottleneck for capable models. Different capability levels require fundamentally different research directions: smaller models need better planning, larger models need better visual perception.

title: MicroCharNet: Less is More for License Plate Character Detection
summary: License plate character detection is a crucial component of intelligent transportation systems, where high accuracy and computational efficiency are required for real-time deployment. Although recent deep learning-based methods have substantially improved detection performance, many high-accuracy models rely on large-scale architectures that incur substantial computational overhead, limiting their applicability to resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose MicroCharNet, an ultra-lightweight model specifically designed for license plate character detection. The proposed architecture employs a compact backbone composed of C2f blocks, integrated with CoordAtt module to enhance feature extraction while preserving spatial information. A lightweight C3k2-based neck fuses multi-level features, followed by a single-level anchor-free detection head that enables end-to-end prediction. Experiments conducted on the UFPR-ALPR dataset demonstrate that MicroCharNet achieves competitive detection accuracy with only 0.08M parameters and 0.096 GFLOPs, while outperforming several recent YOLO-based baselines. Hardware-level evaluations further confirm its efficiency for real-time deployment on edge devices. These results indicate that carefully designed ultra-lightweight architectures can effectively balance accuracy and efficiency in license plate character detection. The source code is available at https://github.com/chequanghuy/MicroCharNet.

AI.tldr: MicroCharNet is an ultra-lightweight model (0.08M parameters, 0.096 GFLOPs) for license plate character detection that uses C2f blocks, CoordAtt module, C3k2-based neck, and an anchor-free detection head to achieve competitive accuracy while enabling real-time deployment on edge devices.
AI.motivation: Existing deep learning-based license plate character detection methods achieve high accuracy but rely on large-scale architectures with substantial computational overhead, limiting deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
AI.method: Proposes MicroCharNet with a compact backbone of C2f blocks integrated with CoordAtt module for enhanced feature extraction with spatial preservation, a lightweight C3k2-based neck for multi-level feature fusion, and a single-level anchor-free detection head for end-to-end prediction.
AI.result: Achieves competitive detection accuracy on UFPR-ALPR dataset with only 0.08M parameters and 0.096 GFLOPs, outperforming several recent YOLO-based baselines, and demonstrates real-time efficiency on edge devices via hardware-level evaluations.
AI.conclusion: Carefully designed ultra-lightweight architectures can effectively balance accuracy and efficiency for license plate character detection in resource-constrained environments.

title: Cycle-World: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Long-term Video World Models via Reverse-Prediction Cycle Consistency
summary: Autoregressive diffusion models have enabled high-quality video generation, yet their sequential nature inherently suffers from error accumulation. In long-horizon video synthesis, minor prediction deviations compound over time, inevitably leading to unconstrained generative drift, structural collapse, and severe visual degradation. To address this, we propose Cycle-World, a novel framework designed for stable and temporally consistent long-video generation. Our approach tackles error drift by enforcing strict temporal reversibility across both the training and inference phases. Theoretically, we demonstrate that forward generative drift can be strictly bottlenecked by a cycle-consistency objective. During training, we integrate an efficient reverse-prediction model to implicitly embed causal constraints into the forward generator, compelling it to produce reversible sequences that tightly adhere to the natural video manifold. At inference time, we repurpose this frozen reverse model as a runtime corrector. Through gradient-based cycle guidance, it iteratively refines the generated latent representations, actively suppressing accumulated errors before they are committed to the historical context. Extensive experiments on the VBench benchmark demonstrate that Cycle-World's dual-phase synergy significantly mitigates error drift, achieving state-of-the-art overall generation quality and long-horizon temporal consistency in 60-second synthesis.

AI.tldr: Cycle-World proposes a framework for long-horizon video generation that enforces temporal reversibility via cycle-consistency during training and gradient-based cycle guidance during inference to mitigate error accumulation and generative drift.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive diffusion models suffer from error accumulation in long-horizon video synthesis, where minor prediction deviations compound over time, leading to generative drift, structural collapse, and visual degradation.
AI.method: Cycle-World enforces strict temporal reversibility through (1) a cycle-consistency objective during training with a reverse-prediction model that embeds causal constraints into the forward generator, and (2) gradient-based cycle guidance during inference that repurposes the frozen reverse model as a runtime corrector to iteratively refine latent representations.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art overall generation quality and long-horizon temporal consistency in 60-second video synthesis on the VBench benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Dual-phase synergy of cycle-consistency training and cycle-guided inference significantly mitigates error drift in long-video generation.

title: HASTE: A Platform for Rapid Post-Disaster Building Damage Assessment
summary: When a large disaster strikes, responders need a map of which buildings are damaged within hours. The models that do well on public benchmarks assume matched before-and-after imagery and a training set drawn from similar past events, and neither is usually available for a new disaster in its first day. We present HASTE (High-speed Assessment and Satellite Tracking for Emergencies), a no-code web platform that lets analysts who are not machine learning engineers produce per-building damage maps from post-disaster satellite imagery. HASTE implements two methods that share one interface. The first requires the user to label polygons over the post-disaster scene, trains a small semantic segmentation model on that single scene, runs it over the whole image, and joins the per-pixel output to existing building footprints. The second embeds every footprint with a pretrained vision model, requires the user to label a handful of buildings, and fits a logistic regression in the browser that scores the rest of the scene in seconds. We describe the platform, both methods, and the engineering that supports them. We also report preliminary experiments on xBD showing that foundation-model embeddings pooled over footprints separate damaged from intact buildings using post-disaster imagery alone, matching a fully supervised ResNet-50 baseline with a twentieth of its labels. HASTE and its predecessors have supported more than thirty real-world disaster responses since 2023, spanning earthquakes, hurricanes, cyclones, floods, wildfires, and tornadoes, delivering results to humanitarian partners within hours to days of imagery becoming available. We close with the directions we think are most promising, including vision-language assessment, active learning, and damage models for roads and other infrastructure. HASTE is open source at https://github.com/microsoft/haste.

AI.tldr: HASTE is a no-code web platform that enables non-ML analysts to produce per-building damage maps from post-disaster satellite imagery using two methods (on-the-fly segmentation training and embedding-based logistic regression), supporting 30+ real-world disaster responses since 2023.
AI.motivation: Large disaster response needs building damage maps within hours, but existing models require matched before-and-after imagery and training data from similar past events, which are unavailable in the first day of a new disaster.
AI.method: Two methods sharing one interface: (1) user labels polygons, trains a small semantic segmentation model on that single scene, runs it over the whole image, joins output to building footprints; (2) embeds each footprint with a pretrained vision model, user labels a few buildings, fits logistic regression in the browser to score the rest. Built as a no-code web platform.
AI.result: Foundation-model embeddings pooled over footprints separate damaged from intact buildings using only post-disaster imagery, matching a fully supervised ResNet-50 baseline with 1/20th the labels. Deployed in 30+ real-world responses since 2023 (earthquakes, hurricanes, cyclones, floods, wildfires, tornadoes).
AI.conclusion: Promising future directions include vision-language assessment, active learning, and damage models for roads and other infrastructure. HASTE is open source.

title: LoRA-Based Cascaded Multimodal Fusion for Action Recognition in Medical Training Environments
summary: This paper presents a cascaded Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)-based multimodal fusion framework for action and activity recognition in healthcare-oriented training environments. The proposed architecture combines parameter-efficient modality-specific adaptation with sequential fusion, enabling modalities to be integrated in stages without retraining previously learned components. Rather than assuming a fixed fusion structure, the framework first integrates more closely related modalities and then incorporates additional heterogeneous modalities, supporting scalable adaptation across datasets with different modality sets.We evaluate the framework on two healthcare-oriented training environment datasets: NurViD and the Nurse Training dataset. Across these datasets, preliminary results suggest that the proposed cascaded fusion strategy improves over individual modality models and provides competitive performance relative to previously reported dataset-specific baselines. Overall, these findings indicate that cascaded LoRA-based fusion is a promising parameter-efficient approach for integrating heterogeneous modalities in medical training action and activity recognition tasks. github: https://github.com/anonymous0-ai/LoRA-Based-Cascaded-Multimodal-Fusion-.git.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a cascaded LoRA-based multimodal fusion framework for action/activity recognition in healthcare training, which incrementally integrates modalities without retraining, achieving competitive results on NurViD and Nurse Training datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal fusion methods for healthcare training action recognition often assume a fixed fusion structure and require retraining when new modalities are added, lacking parameter efficiency and scalability across datasets with different modality sets.
AI.method: A cascaded LoRA-based fusion framework that integrates modalities sequentially: first fusing closely related modalities, then incorporating additional heterogeneous modalities. Each stage uses Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for parameter-efficient fine-tuning without retraining previously learned components.
AI.result: Evaluated on NurViD and Nurse Training datasets; the cascaded fusion strategy outperforms individual modality models and achieves competitive performance compared to previously reported dataset-specific baselines.
AI.conclusion: Cascaded LoRA-based fusion is a promising parameter-efficient approach for integrating heterogeneous modalities in medical training action and activity recognition tasks, supporting scalable adaptation without full retraining.

title: Beyond the Single Camera: Agentic Multi-View Reasoning in Sports Video Understanding
summary: Recent Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance on single-view video understanding benchmarks. However, sports videos involve dense occlusion, rapid motion, and complex interactions that are difficult to resolve from a single viewpoint. In practice, sports events are recorded from multiple camera angles, providing complementary evidence used by referees. Yet, no existing benchmark evaluates MLLMs on multi-view sports video understanding. To address this gap, we introduce SportMV-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark built from official match recordings, through a dedicated pipeline combining LLM-based generation, MLLM-based verification, and human filtering to ensure quality and consistency. SportMV-Bench containing 787 multi-view video bundles and 2592 question-answer pairs across three categories: Perception-Aware Recognition (PAR), Rule-aware Event Interpretation (REI), and Adjudicative Decision Reasoning(ADR). Our analysis shows that current MLLMs fail to effectively exploit multi-view information, with the bottlenecks lying in fine-grained visual perception and view selection rather than logical reasoning or domain knowledge. We propose SportMV-Agent, an agentic framework that orchestrates an iterative loop of active view selection, perception tool execution, and evidence-grounded reasoning, achieving a significant 14.46% relative improvement over the strongest MLLM baseline.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SportMV-Bench, the first benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on multi-view sports video understanding, and SportMV-Agent, an agentic framework that achieves 14.46% relative improvement over existing MLLMs by iteratively selecting views, executing perception tools, and performing evidence-grounded reasoning.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLMs perform well on single-view video understanding but struggle with multi-view sports videos due to dense occlusion, rapid motion, and complex interactions. Despite sports events being recorded from multiple camera angles, no benchmark evaluates MLLMs on multi-view sports video understanding.
AI.method: Built SportMV-Bench using a pipeline with LLM-based generation, MLLM-based verification, and human filtering, resulting in 787 multi-view video bundles and 2592 QA pairs across three categories (PAR, REI, ADR). Proposed SportMV-Agent: an agentic framework with iterative active view selection, perception tool execution, and evidence-grounded reasoning.
AI.result: Current MLLMs fail to exploit multi-view information effectively; bottlenecks are in fine-grained visual perception and view selection, not logical reasoning or domain knowledge. SportMV-Agent achieved 14.46% relative improvement over the strongest MLLM baseline.
