AI.conclusion: Multi-view sports video understanding remains a significant challenge for MLLMs, and the proposed SportMV-Agent demonstrates that explicit view selection and evidence-grounded reasoning can substantially improve performance.

title: Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering
summary: Current Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) excel in question answering (QA) but largely operate as black boxes, providing textual answers without verifiable visual grounding. Existing explainability efforts rely on textual rationales or sparse bounding boxes, which struggle to capture complex video dynamics such as occlusions and non-rigid deformations. We propose Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering (E-VQA), a novel task requiring models to jointly output a semantic answer and precise spatio-temporal evidence: temporal segments and dense, tracked object segmentation masklets. To support this, we introduce ST-Evidence, the first human-verified benchmark for both discriminative and generative pixel-level grounding. Evaluations of state-of-the-art models reveal a critical decoupling between QA accuracy and true visual perception that scaling alone fails to bridge. To address this, we develop scalable, automated generation pipelines to create ST-Evidence-Instruct, a 160k-scale dataset bridging high-level reasoning with fine-grained grounding. Fine-tuning grounded Video LLMs on this data yields substantial gains over the corresponding size-matched UniPixel baselines (e.g., +27.2 t-mean and +13.8 J&F on a 7B model), establishing a robust baseline for explainable, evidence-backed video understanding. Code and data are available at https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/EVQA.

AI.tldr: E-VQA introduces a video QA task requiring models to output answers with spatio-temporal evidence (temporal segments + dense object masklets). A human-verified benchmark (ST-Evidence) and a 160k-scale training dataset (ST-Evidence-Instruct) are created. Fine-tuning grounded Video LLMs yields significant gains (+27.2 t-mean, +13.8 J&F on 7B model) over baselines, establishing a robust baseline for explainable video understanding.
AI.motivation: Current Video LLMs lack verifiable visual grounding, producing answers without explainable evidence. Existing explainability methods (text rationales, sparse bounding boxes) fail to capture complex video dynamics like occlusions and non-rigid deformations.
AI.method: (1) Proposes E-VQA task requiring joint output of semantic answer + spatio-temporal evidence (temporal segments + dense tracked segmentation masklets). (2) Constructs ST-Evidence, the first human-verified benchmark for pixel-level grounding. (3) Develops automated pipelines to generate ST-Evidence-Instruct, a 160k-scale training dataset. (4) Fine-tunes grounded Video LLMs on this dataset.
AI.result: State-of-the-art models show a decoupling between QA accuracy and visual perception that scaling alone cannot fix. Fine-tuning on ST-Evidence-Instruct yields substantial gains over UniPixel baselines (+27.2 t-mean and +13.8 J&F on a 7B model).
AI.conclusion: E-VQA establishes a robust baseline for explainable, evidence-backed video understanding, demonstrating that explicit spatio-temporal grounding training is necessary to bridge the gap between high-level reasoning and fine-grained visual perception.

title: Read It Back: Pretrained MLLMs Are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Text-to-Image Generation
summary: In this paper, we propose SpectraReward, a training-free reward function that turns pretrained MLLMs into off-the-shelf reward models for image-generation reinforcement learning. Instead of asking the MLLM to judge a generated image or answer decomposed verification questions, SpectraReward measures how well the original prompt can be recovered from the generated image through a single image-conditioned, teacher-forced forward pass. We use the average image-conditioned prompt log-likelihood as the reward, directly reusing the MLLM's pretrained image-text alignment ability without preference labels, reward-model fine-tuning. We further introduce Self-SpectraReward, a special case for unified multimodal models where the policy's own understanding branch serves as the reward model for its generation branch, forming a closed-loop self-improving framework without external reward models or external knowledge. Extensive experiments validate SpectraReward through a broad image-generation RL study covering two diffusion models, three RL algorithms, nine reward MLLM backbones from four MLLM families spanning 4B to 235B parameters, and five out-of-distribution text-to-image benchmarks. Results show that both SpectraReward and Self-SpectraReward significantly and consistently improve generation performance and outperform prior MLLM-derived reward training methods. Further analysis reveals that larger reward MLLMs are not always better, while Self-SpectraReward can match or surpass much larger external reward models, suggesting that reward-policy alignment is a key factor for effective image-generation RL. Project Page: https://huangrh99.github.io/SpectraReward/

AI.tldr: SpectraReward is a training-free reward function that uses pretrained MLLMs to measure image-text alignment via prompt recovery likelihood, improving image-generation RL without fine-tuning or preference labels. Self-SpectraReward enables closed-loop self-improvement using the policy model's own understanding branch.
AI.motivation: To enable effective reward signals for image-generation reinforcement learning without requiring preference labels, reward model fine-tuning, or external supervision, by leveraging the inherent image-text alignment capabilities of pretrained MLLMs.
AI.method: SpectraReward computes the average image-conditioned prompt log-likelihood via a single teacher-forced forward pass of a pretrained MLLM, measuring how well the original prompt can be recovered from the generated image. Self-SpectraReward uses the policy's own understanding branch (for unified multimodal models) as the reward model for its generation branch.
AI.result: Both SpectraReward and Self-SpectraReward consistently outperform prior MLLM-derived reward training methods across diverse settings (2 diffusion models, 3 RL algorithms, 9 MLLM backbones from 4B to 235B parameters, 5 benchmarks). Larger reward MLLMs are not always better; Self-SpectraReward matches or surpasses much larger external reward models.
AI.conclusion: Reward-policy alignment is a key factor for effective image-generation RL, and training-free prompt log-likelihood rewards offer a scalable, efficient alternative to fine-tuned reward models or larger external models.
